# MCP reference

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:reference` (scripts/docs-reference.ts); edit the code or scripts/reference/, not this file. -->

tabularius's MCP server offers tools, resource templates and prompts to AI apps. Tool names, descriptions, parameters and hints below are read from the server itself (packages/server/src/mcp.ts and mcp-design.ts); the permissions and examples are checked against the code that runs each tool. For setting up an AI app, see [Connect an AI app](../connect-ai.md).

## Connecting

- **Streamable HTTP** at `/mcp` on the server (`tabularius serve`). Each request gets a fresh, stateless MCP server; replies are JSON (`enableJsonResponse`), so send `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`.
- **stdio**: `tabularius mcp <folder> [--account A]` (password in `TABULARIUS_PASSWORD`), for desktop AI apps that start the server themselves. Without `--account` it acts as the server administrator.

## Who the client is

At `/mcp` the `Authorization` header decides (packages/server/src/index.ts):

| Credential | Acts as |
| --- | --- |
| `Basic` account and password | That account, in every file it names, within its privilege set. The password is checked in each file (and counts toward sign-in lockout). |
| `Bearer ohbt_…` (a file's API token) | One account of that file, its privilege set narrowed to the token's scope (read-only, some layouts). A token limited to some surfaces must include AI apps (`fmmcp`), and the account's sign-in location rules apply. |
| `Bearer ohm_…` (made in the admin console's Connect an AI app) | The account it was made for, in the one file it was made for, until it expires. |
| `Bearer` the server's `--mcp-token`, or the token in the hosted folder's `.openhbam-mcp-token` when none is given (`tabularius mcp-token <folder>` prints it) | The server administrator. |

Anything else gets `401` with `{"error":"unauthorized"}`.

Before authentication, a request with an `Origin` header must match the origin of `--public-url`, or, without it, the connection scheme and Host (a loopback name or IP literal). Other DNS names require the public URL, a `--https` domain, or an explicit allowlist entry. `serve --mcp-origin https://files.example.com` (repeatable, or `TABULARIUS_MCP_ORIGINS`, comma separated) and the server option `mcpAllowedOrigins` list additional origins; authentication still applies. Forwarded host/protocol headers do not grant access. HTTP and HTTPS are distinct; default ports are normalized. Requests without Origin are allowed through this check. A refused origin gets `403` with `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32000,"message":"Invalid Origin header"},"id":null}`.

Every tool that names a file (a `database`, `from` or `to` argument) first checks, for that file, that:

- the account's privilege set has the **fmmcp** extended privilege (AI access; [Full Access] has it), and its password is right;
- AI is not turned off for the file (by the file's own setting, or `--ai-exclude`), nor for any file it uses data from — this applies to the administrator too.

An account sees only the layouts, scripts, records and fields its privilege set allows. Tools that see the whole file (`sql_query`, free-form calculations) need a set that can read every table and field; tools that show the solution's design need [Full Access] or a set that can modify scripts and read everything, and the design-mode tools (packages/server/src/mcp-design.ts) need [Full Access]. Scoped API tokens get none of these. The administrator has no privilege set and may do everything, except in files closed to AI. The **Permissions** line of each tool says what it checks beyond this.

A field can be **masked** for a privilege set: the account sees only a stand-in (its last four characters, or a fixed text; only text and number fields show their last characters, other types show the fixed text) and never the value. A masked field is listed as `masked` and read-only, comes back as its stand-in in records, and cannot be written, searched, sorted, grouped, totalled or charted by; formulas read it as empty. Tools that read every table and field (`sql_query`, `evaluate_calculation`, `check_record` and the like) are refused to an account with a masked field. Masking is applied first; personal data isolation then works on top of it.

**Personal data isolation**: for a file that has it turned on, every tool outside a fixed list (mainly record tools such as `find_records`, `get_record`, `create_record`, plus schema, security and design-reading tools such as `describe_database` and `who_can_access`) is refused, and each refusal is logged. The tools it allows show personal values as stand-ins such as `<PERSON_1>`.

A failed check, like any tool error, comes back as a result with `isError: true` and the message as its text.

## Calling a tool

```http
POST /mcp
Authorization: Basic YWRhOnNlY3JldA==
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json, text/event-stream
MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-06-18

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"list_databases","arguments":{}}}
```

The examples below show each call's `arguments` and the text of the result's first content item (`result.content[0].text`), pretty-printed when it is JSON.

## Tools

| Tool | Hints | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`list_databases`](#list-databases) | read-only | List hosted databases. |
| [`describe_database`](#describe-database) | read-only | Schema of a database: tables and fields, table occurrences, layouts, scripts, value lists, custom functions, privilege sets. |
| [`explain_access`](#explain-access) | read-only | Exactly what a privilege set may do in a database, as ground truth to answer questions about access ("can the Sales set delete invoices?", "which tables can Data Entry see?"). |
| [`who_can_access`](#who-can-access) | read-only | Who can see a table or one field: which accounts of a database can view, change, add to or delete from it, grouped by privilege set, with a plain-English summary ("Sales (ann, bob) can see all records, change some records..."). |
| [`preview_privilege_set`](#preview-privilege-set) | read-only | Validate a proposed privilege set and show, in plain English, how it differs from an existing set (or from no access, when it is new) — never saving it. |
| [`get_script`](#get-script) | read-only | A script as FileMaker shows it in the script workspace, one step per line, indented. |
| [`run_script`](#run-script) | destructive, open world | Run a FileMaker script on the server, as FileMaker Server runs it for the Data API: no dialogs (Show Custom Dialog picks the first button and is listed in actions), no screen. |
| [`debug_script`](#debug-script) | destructive | Run a script under the debugger, as Script Debugger and Data Viewer do, offline (no network, mail or plug-ins, whatever the server allows people): it stops at each breakpoint (and at errors with pauseOnError), records where it is, its variables and the watch formulas evaluated there, then carries on. |
| [`explain_script_failure`](#explain-script-failure) | read-only | Why a script stopped with an error: it runs again on a throwaway copy of the file, offline (nothing is sent or changed), as this account, from the layout and record it ran on. |
| [`find_records`](#find-records) | read-only | Find records through a layout using FileMaker find requests. |
| [`get_record`](#get-record) | read-only | Read one record by record id. |
| [`describe_record`](#describe-record) | read-only | One record with what hangs off it, for summarizing it or answering questions about it: its fields with values (calculations worked out; empty ones listed), and for each relationship one step from the layout's table occurrence, how it matches, how many related records there are and the first few (orders, notes, line items). |
| [`create_record`](#create-record) |  | Create a record. |
| [`update_record`](#update-record) | idempotent | Change fields of a record, and its portal rows: portalData edits rows by recordId or adds rows without one; deleteRelated removes rows ("Portal.recordId"). |
| [`update_records`](#update-records) | destructive | Set the same fields on every record a find gives (up to 1,000), as this account, all or none: a record that cannot take the value (a rule, a lock, a privilege) stops the whole change. |
| [`upload_container`](#upload-container) | destructive | Put a file (image, PDF, anything) in a container field of a record, as Insert File does. |
| [`evaluate_calculation`](#evaluate-calculation) | read-only | Evaluate a FileMaker calculation formula in a layout's context, optionally on one record (fields, related fields through the relationship graph, custom functions, Get functions, ExecuteSQL). |
| [`delete_record`](#delete-record) | destructive | Delete a record. |
| [`revert_change`](#revert-change) | destructive | Put back what one entry of a record's audit log changed (the seq numbers come from explain_record_history, where each change carries its seq): an edit gets its old values again (fields picks some), a created record is deleted, a deleted record is made again under its id. |
| [`get_container`](#get-container) | read-only | Contents of a container field (image, PDF or file). |
| [`sql_query`](#sql-query) | read-only | Run read-only SQL (SQLite dialect) for analysis across tables. |
| [`explain_solution`](#explain-solution) | read-only | A readable map of a solution: its tables (record counts, keys, layouts), relationships, script folders, which scripts buttons start, which are never called, the most called ones, and which reach outside (mail, network, plug-ins). |
| [`solution_map`](#solution-map) | read-only | A cross-file map of a multi-file solution: which hosted files' table occurrences, value lists and scripts reach into which other files, plus any external references whose file is not hosted (a red reference in FileMaker). |
| [`document_solution`](#document-solution) | read-only | Documentation of a solution as Markdown: every table with its fields (types, formulas, auto-enter, comments), the relationships, each layout (its table, fields, the scripts its buttons and triggers run) and each script (its own header comment, what starts it, what it calls, the layouts it goes to, whether it reaches outside). |
| [`where_used`](#where-used) | read-only | Every place that uses a field ("Table::Field" or "Occurrence::Field"), script, layout, table, table occurrence, custom function or value list: calculations, auto-enter and validation, script steps, layout objects (fields, buttons, hide conditions, conditional formatting) and relationships. |
| [`search_solution`](#search-solution) | read-only | Search the whole design: table, field, layout, script, value list and custom function names, field comments, every formula, every script line and layout text. |
| [`describe_layout`](#describe-layout) | read-only | Fields on a layout, as find_records names them, with type, value list values, how many records have a value, ranges (numbers, dates) and the common or example values, related and portal fields included (find_records searches them as Occurrence::Field); plus its portals. |
| [`check_calculation`](#check-calculation) | read-only | Check a drafted FileMaker formula in a layout's context without changing data: syntax errors with FileMaker's error code, unknown fields, table occurrences and functions (with "did you mean"), wrong parameter counts, and the result on the first few records. |
| [`explain_value`](#explain-value) | read-only | Why a field holds the value it does on a record: its formula (calculation or auto-enter), the value of every field it reads, each step of the evaluation with its intermediate result, whether "Do not evaluate if all referenced fields are empty" kept it empty, whether the stored value still matches the formula, the chain of calculations behind it, and lint warnings. |
| [`check_record`](#check-record) | read-only | Why does this record look wrong? |
| [`explain_related`](#explain-related) | read-only | Why a portal or related field on a record shows what it does (or nothing): the relationship path followed, each match field with its values on both sides and how many records each finds on its own, the portal's filter and sort, every related record with whether it is shown and why, and a one-line verdict ("empty because Customers::Id is empty on this record"). |
| [`lint_formulas`](#lint-formulas) | read-only | Warnings for every calculation and auto-enter formula in a file (or one table): text fields in arithmetic, dates compared with text, "Do not evaluate if all referenced fields are empty" hiding the result the formula was written for (IsEmpty flags, defaults) or not applying (formulas reading containers), stored calculations reading globals or related records, unused Let variables, missing fields. |
| [`check_script`](#check-script) | read-only | Check a drafted script without running it. |
| [`search_records`](#search-records) | read-only | Search the text of every record, in every table, for words, best matches first, like a site search: "acme march invoice" finds records whose text fields hold those words, in any field. |
| [`semantic_find`](#semantic-find) | read-only | Find records by meaning, best matches first: "customers unhappy about late delivery" finds records whose stored embedding is closest to the question, even with none of those words. |
| [`summarize_records`](#summarize-records) | read-only | Totals of a found set, overall or broken down by up to 3 fields, like a sub-summary report: count of records, and sum, average, min, max, count or distinct count of fields. |
| [`list_dashboards`](#list-dashboards) | read-only | Dashboards saved in a file: charts, summary tables and numbers worked out live from finds. |
| [`get_dashboard`](#get-dashboard) | read-only | A saved dashboard (by id or name) with each widget worked out now, as this account: its find in words (relative dates with the range they mean today), its grouping, and its numbers. |
| [`save_dashboard`](#save-dashboard) |  | Save a dashboard in a file from a plain-English request: "revenue by month for my top 10 customers this year" is a line chart on an Invoices layout, query [{"Date": "this year"}], groupBy ["Date", "Customer"], by "month", measure sum of Amount, top {field: "Customer", n: 10}, plus a table of the same grouped by Customer. |
| [`find_data_problems`](#find-data-problems) | read-only | Data cleanup, step one (changes nothing): likely duplicate records on a layout (the same email or phone, names nearly alike with the same address), values not in the field's value list ("Actve" for "Active"), and malformed phone numbers and email addresses, each with a suggested fix where there is a likely one. |
| [`fix_data_problems`](#fix-data-problems) | destructive | Data cleanup, step two: apply fixes ({field, from, to}: every record with that value gets the new one) and merges ({keep, remove: [ids], fill?}: the kept record gets fill for its empty fields, related records move to it, the others are deleted), from find_data_problems, all or none, as this account. |
| [`plan_import`](#plan-import) | read-only | Importing a spreadsheet, step one: match a CSV's columns to a layout's fields (by name and by what the values look like), with the fixes each column needs (date order, currency and thousands separators, yes/no, value list spellings, Excel dates, phone numbers, a full name or "City, ST 12345" split across several fields), a preview of what rows become with any problems, and rows that repeat a record already in the table or an earlier row (by keys: an email, an id or code). |
| [`import_records`](#import-records) |  | Importing a spreadsheet, step two: each row becomes a new record of the layout's table, as this account, with the columns, fixes and keys from plan_import. |
| [`undo_import`](#undo-import) | destructive | Takes back an import from import_records (or the web client): deletes the records it made, except ones changed since. |
| [`undo_data_fix`](#undo-data-fix) | destructive | Undo a batch fix_data_problems applied (by its id), all or none: values set back and merged records put back. |
| [`find_stale_calcs`](#find-stale-calcs) | read-only | Stored calculations whose saved value is no longer what the formula gives now, with counts per field (changes nothing). |
| [`refresh_stale_calcs`](#refresh-stale-calcs) | destructive | Bring chosen stored calculations up to date (from find_stale_calcs): every record, or the ones listed, whose stored value differs from what the formula gives now gets the new value, all or none. |
| [`undo_stale_refresh`](#undo-stale-refresh) | destructive | Undo a batch refresh_stale_calcs made (by its id): the stored values it replaced are put back, except where they changed again since. |
| [`list_automations`](#list-automations) | read-only | Automations in a file: what sets each off (records created or changed, a field changed, a condition) and the script it runs on the record, with its recent runs. |
| [`try_automation`](#try-automation) | read-only | Automations in plain English, step one: "when an invoice is marked paid, set the paid date and add a note to the customer" is on "update", fields ["Status"], condition Status = "Paid", and a script that sets PaidDate and creates the note. |
| [`save_automation`](#save-automation) | destructive | Automations, step two: save (and turn on) an automation tried with try_automation, writing its script if scriptText is given. |
| [`delete_automation`](#delete-automation) | destructive | Delete an automation (by name or id). |
| [`list_connections`](#list-connections) | read-only | The outside services this server can connect to, by name (S3-compatible storage: Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, MinIO, Wasabi; REST web APIs; and email accounts for Send Mail): each one's settings, whether it is a draft (waiting for a person), on or off, which files may use it, and which of its secrets are set (never their values). |
| [`draft_connection`](#draft-connection) |  | Set up a connection to an outside service from what the person asked ("set up an S3 connection to our invoices bucket"): this makes a DRAFT with the settings they gave (type, bucket, region, endpoint for R2/B2/MinIO, a folder in the bucket) and nothing else. |
| [`conversion_report`](#conversion-report) | read-only | What in a converted FileMaker file won't work yet in Tabularius: script steps the engine can't run, FileMaker functions not available yet, plug-in functions, formulas that don't parse, other files the solution uses that aren't hosted, and accounts without a password. |
| [`conversion_guide`](#conversion-guide) | read-only | The plain-English guide to a converted file, written when it was converted (or converted again): what won't work until changed (plug-ins, steps and functions not available yet, tables in SQL databases, other files not hosted), what works differently (Send Mail sends nothing, Insert from URL stays offline, web viewers that load internet pages show a placeholder, screen-only steps skipped on the server, privilege sets imported at the whole-file level), the built-in replacement for each, and what to do before people use it. |
| [`optimization_report`](#optimization-report) | read-only | Ways to make a converted file smaller and faster, worst first, each with what it would save and what to do: container files kept inside the file (size by field: S3 or managed external storage instead, and only a link kept), sorts and matches on unstored calculations or fields without an index in big tables, fields, scripts, table occurrences and value lists nothing uses, wide tables, repeating fields, long value lists. |
| [`optimization_fix`](#optimization-fix) | destructive | Makes one of the fixes optimization_report offers for a hosted file: hide or remove the scripts, value lists or table occurrences nothing uses, or store an unstored calculation a sort depends on. |
| [`optimization_move_containers`](#optimization-move-containers) | destructive | Moves the container files a converted file keeps inside its database (the optimization report names the fields) out to managed external storage: one file each, in the field's folder beside the hosted file, and the file is then rewritten so it shrinks. |
| [`migration_plan`](#migration-plan) | read-only | Moving a converted file off its plug-ins (360Works Email, MBS, BaseElements, Troi, DataGuard, ...): every plug-in call, grouped by plug-in, with how often and where, whether it works here already, and the native FileMaker replacement (Send Mail via SMTP for mail plug-ins, Insert from URL for HTTP, JSON and Crypt functions, data file steps). |
| [`compare_solutions`](#compare-solutions) | read-only | Compare two hosted databases, usually two versions of one solution (staged against live, a backup against today's file): tables, fields (type, formula, options), table occurrences, relationships, layouts (fields and buttons on them), scripts (with a line diff), value lists, custom functions, accounts, privilege sets and record counts that were added, removed, renamed or changed. |
| [`get_design`](#get-design) | read-only | Design of a database for design work, with ids: tables with every field option, table occurrences, relationships with match fields, File Options (startup layout and scripts), value lists, custom functions, custom menus, layouts, scripts as text. |
| [`get_theme`](#get-theme) | read-only | A theme in full: element defaults and every named style, each as rules (part, state, css). |
| [`get_layout_design`](#get-layout-design) | read-only | A layout's design as stored: parts (kind, top, height), objects (kind, bounds in points, field, text, portal, button action, styles, conditions), table view columns. |
| [`lint_script`](#lint-script) | read-only | Check scripts for loops that never end and guards that catch nothing, which FileMaker never warns about: a loop with no way out (Go to Record [ Next ] without “Exit after last”), Exit Loop If [ $count = $i ] when $i starts at 1 and the count can be 0, a loop that omits records and only ends on “Exit after last” in another branch, and IsValid used to ask whether there is a related record. |
| [`lint_layout`](#lint-layout) | read-only | Check a layout for what will look or behave wrong in Browse mode: fields showing <Field Missing> or nothing (occurrence not related to the layout's), objects outside the layout, clickable objects on top of each other, buttons with no action, enterable fields left out of the tab order, and fields some privilege sets see as <No Access>; rule "slow" is what makes the layout slow to draw (unstored related totals, summaries on every row, portal filters), with cost = estimated record reads per draw from the file's record counts. |
| [`check_solution`](#check-solution) | read-only | Look through the whole solution for what is wrong, without running anything: calculations that do not parse or name a field, function, script, layout or value list that is not there; layout objects and relationships that point at a deleted field; value lists with no source; script steps and plug-in functions this build does not run (error 3, or "?"); privilege sets that name things that are gone or grant nothing; accounts with no privilege set; and, as information only, scripts, value lists and custom functions nothing uses. |
| [`fix_layout`](#fix-layout) | destructive | Mend lint_layout's mechanical findings on a layout in one change: nearly lined-up edges lined up, clickable objects on top of each other moved apart, objects running past the layout's edge moved inside, and the tab order given the fields it skips (in reading order), fields with no label labelled with their name, buttons with no text given a tooltip naming their script, fields and buttons too small to tap on a phone layout grown, and fields a portal sorts on with indexing off given automatic indexing, and summary fields on every row of a list moved into a trailing grand summary. |
| [`speed_up_layout`](#speed-up-layout) | destructive | Make a slow layout faster (FileMaker has no such tool): for each of lint_layout's "slow" findings, a redesign that removes the work where there is a mechanical one: a summary field on every row moved into a trailing grand summary, an unstored calculation or related summary on every row shown from a new stored calculation (which can fall behind related records; the caveat says so). |
| [`review_graph`](#review-graph) | read-only | Look over the relationship graph: a plain-English account of its groups (and whether it follows anchor-buoy), and the problems worth a look: occurrences nothing uses, relationships that repeat another in the same group, match fields that can't be indexed (globals, unstored calculations, summaries, containers) or have indexing off, and missing tables or fields. |
| [`arrange_graph`](#arrange-graph) | destructive | Tidy the relationship graph's boxes in one change: each group laid out from its anchor (the occurrence layouts are based on) in columns to the right, groups stacked top to bottom, lone occurrences in a grid at the end. |
| [`restyle_layout`](#restyle-layout) | destructive | Restyle a layout: make it look like another layout (its theme, and each kind of object's most common style and formatting, part by part), switch it to a theme, and/or apply the theme consistently (drop local formatting so every object shows its theme style). |
| [`restyle_file`](#restyle-file) | destructive | Restyle every layout in a file at once (FileMaker restyles one layout at a time): onto an existing theme, or onto a new theme made from a few design tokens (accent, accentText, text, muted, background, panel, line: #rrggbb colours; font; size and radius in points; tabularius's own look for any left out). |
| [`modernize_interfaces`](#modernize-interfaces) | destructive | Make new layouts for a file's tables from ready-made templates, with no AI: for each table a modern list, a modern detail (one record with Previous and Next), a modern list and detail side by side (HTML, CSS and JavaScript pages that search, sort, edit, add and delete records as the signed-in account and show related records), and a classic FileMaker list and form drafted the way the file's own layouts look. |
| [`draft_layout`](#draft-layout) | destructive | Draft a new layout that looks like the file's own: the theme most of its layouts use (or like: another layout's), fields, labels, title and parts styled as they most often are there, and the components the file keeps in its headers and footers placed where they usually sit. |
| [`change_design`](#change-design) | destructive | Change a database's design: create, rename, change or delete tables, fields, table occurrences, relationships, value lists, custom functions, layouts and scripts. |
| [`check_formula`](#check-formula) | read-only | Check a calculation formula before using it in change_design, as FileMaker's Specify Calculation dialog does: syntax, field and table occurrence names, function names and parameter counts. |
| [`design_history`](#design-history) | read-only | Design changes made to a database in Tabularius (by people, scripts or AI), oldest first. |
| [`audit_log`](#audit-log) | read-only | Who created, changed and deleted which records of a database, and when, oldest first. |
| [`explain_record_history`](#explain-record-history) | read-only | What changed on one record and why, newest first: changes made together are one event (who, when, each field from and to), each change says how it came about where the design shows it (worked out by an auto-enter calculation from another field changed then, stamped with the modification time or account, looked up from a related record), which automation or data cleanup made it, and what else the same account changed in other tables at that moment. |
| [`suggest_indexes`](#suggest-indexes) | read-only | Slow finds on this server and what would speed them up: each kind of find (table, fields searched, sort) that took 50 ms or more on average since the server started, with its timings, an index to add where a stored field has none (with why), and plain-English hints where no index helps (unstored calculations, criteria starting with *). |
| [`get_security`](#get-security) | read-only | Accounts and privilege sets, as Manage Security shows them: each account's privilege set, whether it has a password (blankPassword: still the file's empty one), a second factor, is external or inactive; each privilege set's record, layout, value list and script access and extended privileges; the password policy; and API tokens (without their secrets). |
| [`review_privileges`](#review-privileges) | read-only | A privilege audit in plain English: risky setups among the accounts and privilege sets, worst first, each as a sentence with where it is and what to do: full-access accounts with no password or only a password, guest access, extended privileges (Data API, OData, ODBC, ...) switched on that no recent sign-in uses, record-level limits that are true for every record, and unstored calculations a limited set can see that read records it can't view. |

| [`try_design_change`](#try-design-change) | read-only | Try design changes (change_design's) on a throwaway copy of the file, then run scripts there once, offline (no network, mail or plug-ins), and report how each run went: steps, the last error and where. |

<a id="list-databases"></a>

### `list_databases`

List hosted databases.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Any identity. Lists only the hosted files it can use (its account signs in and has fmmcp there); files with AI turned off are never listed.

**Parameters:** none

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "list_databases",
  "arguments": {}
}
```

Result:

```json
[
  "Invoices",
  "Contacts"
]
```

<a id="describe-database"></a>

### `describe_database`

Schema of a database: tables and fields, table occurrences, layouts, scripts, value lists, custom functions, privilege sets. Formulas and custom function bodies only for the tables and functions named in detail.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file. Tables, fields, layouts, scripts and value lists are filtered by the privilege set; formulas and custom functions only for sets that can modify scripts; a set other than [Full Access] sees only its own privilege set's name.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `detail` | array of string | no | Table or custom function names to show in full: field formulas and auto-enter calculations, or function bodies (at most 20 items) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "describe_database",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "createdWith": "FileMaker Tabularius",
  "tables": [

          "type": "text",
          "kind": "normal"
        },
        {

          "type": "text",
          "kind": "normal"
        },
        {
          "name": "Email",
          "type": "text",
          "kind": "normal"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "Invoices",
      "fields": [
        {
          "name": "CustomerId",
          "type": "text",
          "kind": "normal"
        },
        {
          "name": "Customer",
          "type": "text",
          "kind": "normal"
        },
        {
          "name": "Amount",
          "type": "number",
          "kind": "normal"
        },
        {
          "name": "Status",
          "type": "text",
          "kind": "normal"
        },
        {
          "name": "Date",
          "type": "date",
          "kind": "normal"
        },
        {
          "name": "Attachment",
          "type": "container",
          "kind": "normal"
        },
        {
          "name": "Total",
          "type": "number",
          "kind": "calculation"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "tableOccurrences": [
    {
      "name": "Customers",
      "baseTable": "Customers"
    },
    {
      "name": "Invoices",
      "baseTable": "Invoices"
    }
  ],
  "layouts": [
    {
      "name": "Customers",

    },
```

A masked field is listed with masked: true and readOnly: true (a hidden one is left out). An account signed in with a password also gets "account" and "privilegeSet" fields. A large file's outline is shortened to one line per field, then to field names only, and the note says so.

<a id="explain-access"></a>

### `explain_access`

Exactly what a privilege set may do in a database, as ground truth to answer questions about access ("can the Sales set delete invoices?", "which tables can Data Entry see?"). Returns the extended privileges, available menu commands, the default record rule, and per table whether the set can view, edit, create and delete, each as yes, no, or a per-record calculation quoted verbatim, plus any fields it can't see or change and any layouts, scripts or value lists that differ from the default. Answer from these facts and cite the exact rule; never guess. Read-only. Omit privilegeSet to report the set this session signed in with.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file. A set other than [Full Access] can explain only its own privilege set; [Full Access] and the server administrator can name any set (the administrator must name one).

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `privilegeSet` | string | no | Privilege set name; defaults to this session's own set |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "explain_access",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "privilegeSet": "[Full Access]"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "privilegeSet": "[Full Access]",
  "fullAccess": true,
  "extendedPrivileges": [
    "(all)"
  ],
  "menuCommands": "all",
  "defaultRecords": {
    "table": "(every other table)",
    "view": {
      "allowed": true
    },
    "edit": {
      "allowed": true
    },
    "create": true,
    "delete": {
      "allowed": true
    }
  },
  "tables": [
    {
      "table": "Customers",
      "view": {
        "allowed": true
      },
      "edit": {
        "allowed": true
      },
      "create": true,
      "delete": {
        "allowed": true
      }
    },
    {
      "table": "Invoices",
      "view": {
        "allowed": true
      },
      "edit": {
        "allowed": true
      },
      "create": true,
      "delete": {
        "allowed": true
      }
    }
  ],
  "layouts": {
    "default": "modifiable",
    "exceptions": []
  },
  "scripts": {
    "default": "modifiable",
    "exceptions": []
  },
  "valueLists": {
    "default": "modifiable",
    "exceptions": []
  }
}
```

<a id="who-can-access"></a>

### `who_can_access`

Who can see a table or one field: which accounts of a database can view, change, add to or delete from it, grouped by privilege set, with a plain-English summary ("Sales (ann, bob) can see all records, change some records..."). A record rule that limits rows reads as "some records". Use it to answer "who can see the salary field?" or to audit exposure before sharing a database. Names accounts, sets and fields only, never record values. Read-only, and only for a full-access session because it lists every account.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] or the server administrator only (it lists every account); any other privilege set is refused, and so is a scoped API token. Names accounts, privilege sets and fields, never record values.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `table` | string | yes | Table name |
| `field` | string | no | A field of that table, to ask about the field alone |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "who_can_access",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "table": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "table": "Invoices",
  "sets": [
    {
      "privilegeSet": "Sales",
      "accounts": [
        "ann",
        "bob"
      ],
      "view": "all records",
      "edit": "all records",
      "create": "yes",
      "delete": "no",
      "hiddenFields": [
        "Salary"
      ],
      "readOnlyFields": [],
      "maskedFields": [],
      "says": "Sales (ann, bob) can see all records, change all records, add new ones and not delete; cannot see Salary."
    },
    {
      "privilegeSet": "Viewers",
      "accounts": [
        "carol"
      ],
      "view": "some records",
      "edit": "no",
      "create": "no",
      "delete": "no",
      "hiddenFields": [],
      "readOnlyFields": [],
      "maskedFields": [],
      "says": "Viewers (carol) can see some records, not change any, not add and not delete."
    }
  ],
  "canSee": [
    "ann",
    "bob",
    "carol"
  ],
  "summary": "3 of 3 active accounts can see Invoices. Sales (ann, bob) can see all records, change all records, add new ones and not delete; cannot see Salary. Viewers (carol) can see some records, not change any, not add and not delete."
}
```

Only accounts that are turned on and have a privilege set count. A record rule on the set ("only its own records") reads as "some records". With field, the answer is about that field alone: sets that can't see it say "cannot see Invoices::Salary", a view-only field can be seen but not changed, a set that sees only a masked version of it is marked masked: true (its accounts are listed in canSeeMasked, not canSee), and hiddenFields, readOnlyFields and create are empty. maskedFields lists the fields a set sees only a stand-in for. An unknown table or field is an error.

<a id="preview-privilege-set"></a>

### `preview_privilege_set`

Validate a proposed privilege set and show, in plain English, how it differs from an existing set (or from no access, when it is new) — never saving it. Use this to turn a request like "a set that can read everything but only edit its own records" into a reviewable diff for an administrator to approve and apply by hand; this tool never changes the file. The proposal has the same shape as a privilege set in describe_database: name, records (view/edit/create/delete, each a boolean or a calculation), layouts, scripts, valueLists, extendedPrivileges, optional menuCommands and per-table overrides. Read-only.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] or the server administrator. Read-only: it never saves the set.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `proposed` | object of any | yes | The proposed privilege-set definition (same shape describe_database reports) |
| `base` | string | no | Existing privilege set to diff against; defaults to one with the proposed name, else no access |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "preview_privilege_set",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "proposed": {
      "name": "Sales",
      "records": {
        "view": true,
        "edit": "Status = \"Open\"",
        "create": true,
        "delete": false
      },
      "layouts": "viewOnly",
      "scripts": "viewOnly",
      "valueLists": "viewOnly",
      "extendedPrivileges": [
        "fmrest"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "valid": true,
  "changes": [
    {
      "area": "records",
      "detail": "default record access → view yes, edit limited (Status = \"Open\"), create yes, delete no"
    },
    {
      "area": "layouts",
      "detail": "default layouts access → viewOnly"
    },
    {
      "area": "scripts",
      "detail": "default scripts access → viewOnly"
    },
    {
      "area": "valueLists",
      "detail": "default valueLists access → viewOnly"
    },
    {
      "area": "extendedPrivileges",
      "detail": "grant fmrest"
    }
  ]
}
```

<a id="get-script"></a>

### `get_script`

A script as FileMaker shows it in the script workspace, one step per line, indented. Pass detail: true for each step's decoded options (targets, layouts, find requests, sort order).

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file, for a script its privilege set can modify; a script it can only run is refused, and one it has no access to reads as missing. Secrets in the script text are hidden.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `script` | string | yes | The script's name |
| `detail` | boolean | no | true adds each step's decoded options (default false) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "get_script",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "script": "Mark Paid"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "name": "Mark Paid",
  "id": 1,
  "text": "Set Field [ Invoices::Status ; \"Paid\" ]\nExit Script [ Result: \"done\" ]"
}
```

With detail: true the result also has "steps": each step's name, enabled flag and decoded params. A Perform Script step that picks its script by name shows as Perform Script [ Specified: By name ; calculation ] (the calculation gives the name, "File::Script" for another file).

<a id="run-script"></a>

### `run_script`

Run a FileMaker script on the server, as FileMaker Server runs it for the Data API: no dialogs (Show Custom Dialog picks the first button and is listed in actions), no screen. Scripts can create, change and delete records. Returns the Exit Script result, the last error code (0 = none), where it ended, and with trace: true every step that ran with its error code for [Full Access] accounts. Other accounts still run the script, but do not receive the trace.

**Hints:** destructive, open world

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file, for a script (and starting layout) its privilege set can use; the script runs as that account with its privileges. Scripts run offline: no network, mail or AI steps, whatever the server allows people.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `script` | string | yes | The script's name |
| `parameter` | string | no | Get ( ScriptParameter ) |
| `layout` | string | no | Layout to start on; default the first layout |
| `trace` | boolean | no | true lists every step that ran, with its error code (default false) |
| `maxSeconds` | number | no | Stop the script after this many seconds (60 is the most, and the default). One that loops for ever ends then, with the line it was in and, where the script lints it, why. (min 1, max 60) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "run_script",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "script": "Mark Paid",
    "layout": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "result": "done",
  "error": 0,
  "halted": false,
  "layout": "Invoices",
  "foundCount": 3,
  "recordId": 1,
  "foundSet": [
    1,
    2,
    3
  ],
  "mode": "browse",
  "steps": 2,
  "actions": []
}
```

With trace: true the result also has "trace": each step that ran ({script, index, line}). $$variables and global fields last between calls for each file while the server runs. A Perform Script step that picks its script by name (Specified: By name) runs the script its calculation names, matched ignoring case; a name that matches none stops with error 104, and the privilege set must be able to run that script too.

<a id="debug-script"></a>

### `debug_script`

Run a script under the debugger, as Script Debugger and Data Viewer do, offline (no network, mail or plug-ins, whatever the server allows people): it stops at each breakpoint (and at errors with pauseOnError), records where it is, its variables and the watch formulas evaluated there, then carries on. Returns every stop and how the run ended. [Full Access] only. By default it runs on a throwaway copy of the file, so nothing it changes reaches the hosted file; with scratch: false it runs on the hosted file and, like run_script, really changes records.

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** [Full Access] or the server administrator.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `script` | string | yes | The script's name |
| `parameter` | string | no | Get ( ScriptParameter ) |
| `layout` | string | no | Layout to start on |
| `recordId` | integer | no | Record to start on (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |
| `breakpoints` | array of object | no | Steps to stop at, each a step number from 1 (and the script, if not the one run) (default []) |
| `breakpoints[].script` | string | no | Default: the script run |
| `breakpoints[].step` | integer | yes | Step number, from 1 (min 1, max 9007199254740991) |
| `watch` | array of string | no | Formulas to evaluate at each stop (Data Viewer Watch) (default [], at most 20 items) |
| `pauseOnError` | boolean | no | true also stops at each step that sets an error (default false) |
| `maxStops` | integer | no | The run is halted after this many stops (default 20, min 1, max 100) |
| `scratch` | boolean | no | Run on a throwaway copy of the file (default); false runs on the hosted file (default true) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "debug_script",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "script": "Mark Paid",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "breakpoints": [
      {
        "step": 2
      }
    ],
    "watch": [
      "Invoices::Status"
    ]
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "stops": [
    {
      "script": "Mark Paid",
      "step": 2,
      "line": "Exit Script [ Result: \"done\" ]",
      "lastError": 0,
      "layout": "Invoices",
      "foundCount": 3,
      "recordId": 1,
      "variables": {
        "locals": {},
        "globals": {}
      },
      "watch": [
        {
          "formula": "Invoices::Status",
          "value": "Paid"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "scratch": true,
  "result": {
    "result": "done",
    "error": 0,
    "halted": false,
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "foundCount": 3,
    "recordId": 1,
    "foundSet": [
      1,
      2,
      3
    ],
    "mode": "browse",
    "steps": 2,
    "actions": []
  }
}
```

<a id="explain-script-failure"></a>

### `explain_script_failure`

Why a script stopped with an error: it runs again on a throwaway copy of the file, offline (nothing is sent or changed), as this account, from the layout and record it ran on. Returns the step that set the error and the scripts that called it, the error code and what it means, the variables then, the fields the step names with their values (calculations with their formula and inputs), and hints (a name that is almost right, an empty found set). Read it before suggesting a fix.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access], or a set that can modify scripts and read everything (designAccess), and that may run the script; not available to scoped API tokens.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `script` | string | yes | The script's name |
| `layout` | string | no | Layout it ran from; default where a button or trigger starts it |
| `recordId` | integer | no | Record it ran on (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |
| `parameter` | string | no | Get ( ScriptParameter ) it ran with |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "explain_script_failure",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "script": "Mark Paid",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "recordId": 1
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "script": "Mark Paid",
  "outcome": "ok",
  "error": 0,
  "layout": "Invoices",
  "hints": [
    "It ran to the end with no error here. If it failed for someone, try their layout, record and account: the found set, the record and privileges change what a script does."
  ],
  "ranOn": "a throwaway copy of the file, offline (nothing was sent or changed)"
}
```

Where the step names a calculation field, its inputs come from the same explanation as explain_value: an input the privilege set can't see shows as "‹no access›" instead of its value.

<a id="find-records"></a>

### `find_records`

Find records through a layout using FileMaker find requests. Omit query to list all records. Each record shows its first 5 portal rows (portalTotals says how many there are in all); ask for more with portalRows, or name the portal's fields in fields.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file. Layouts, records and fields are filtered by the privilege set; values of password, key and token fields are hidden and long values cut. A masked field comes back as its stand-in (its last four characters, or a fixed text), never its value.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `layout` | string | yes | Layout name; records are read and written through a layout |
| `query` | array of object of string or number or boolean | no | FileMaker find requests, one object per request, field name to criterion (e.g. [{"Status": "Open"}, {"Status": "Pending"}]); each is ORed; "omit": true on a request leaves its matches out. Leave out for all records (at most 50 items) |
| `sort` | array of object | no | Sort order, most significant first (at most 20 items) |
| `sort[].fieldName` | string | yes |  |
| `sort[].sortOrder` | "ascend" \\| "descend" | no |  |
| `limit` | integer | no | Most results to return (default 50, min 0, max 1000) |
| `offset` | integer | no | 1-based (default 1, min 1, max 9007199254740991) |
| `fields` | array of string | no | Only these fields (and "TO::Field" for portal rows). Values over 500 characters are cut, and password, key and token fields are hidden. (at most 200 items) |
| `portalRows` | integer | no | Portal rows kept per portal (default 5; with fields, all of the rows asked for) (min 0, max 1000) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "find_records",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "query": [
      {
        "Status": "Open"
      }
    ],
    "limit": 2,
    "fields": [
      "Customer",
      "Amount",
      "Status"
    ]
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "records": [
    {
      "recordId": 1,
      "modId": 0,
      "fieldData": {
        "Customer": "Acme Corp",
        "Amount": 1200,
        "Status": "Open"
      }
    }
  ],
  "foundCount": 1,
  "totalCount": 3
}
```

A masked field can't be searched or sorted by (an error). A portal on the layout comes back in each record's "portalData". A portal on the layout's own table occurrence (it shows the found set) reads only Portal Setup's number of rows plus five (10 plus five when none is set), not 50.

<a id="get-record"></a>

### `get_record`

Read one record by record id.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file, for a record its privilege set can view; fields it can't see are left out, a masked field comes back as its stand-in, and values of password, key and token fields are hidden.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `layout` | string | yes | Layout name; records are read and written through a layout |
| `recordId` | integer | yes | The record id, as find_records and get_record show it (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |
| `fields` | array of string | no | Only these fields (and "TO::Field" for portal rows). Values over 500 characters are cut, and password, key and token fields are hidden. (at most 200 items) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "get_record",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "recordId": 1
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "recordId": 1,
  "modId": 0,
  "fieldData": {
    "CustomerId": "C1",
    "Customer": "Acme Corp",
    "Amount": 1200,
    "Status": "Open",
    "Date": "2026-09-01",
    "Attachment": "",
    "Total": 1320
  }
}
```

A portal on the layout comes back in "portalData"; one on the layout's own table occurrence (it shows the found set) reads only Portal Setup's number of rows plus five (10 plus five when none is set), not 50.

<a id="describe-record"></a>

### `describe_record`

One record with what hangs off it, for summarizing it or answering questions about it: its fields with values (calculations worked out; empty ones listed), and for each relationship one step from the layout's table occurrence, how it matches, how many related records there are and the first few (orders, notes, line items). Pass follow to read occurrences further along the graph instead. Only what the account can see. Cite facts as [Occurrence::Field] or [Occurrence::Field #recordId].

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file. The record, its fields and its related records are only those the privilege set can see (in each file). A masked field shows its stand-in, and "masked" lists those fields.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `layout` | string | yes | Layout name; records are read and written through a layout |
| `recordId` | integer | yes | The record id, as find_records and get_record show it (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |
| `limit` | integer | no | Related records listed per relationship (default 5) (min 0, max 50) |
| `follow` | array of string | no | Table occurrences to read related records from, instead of those one step away (at most 25 items) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "describe_record",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "recordId": 1
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "layout": "Invoices",
  "occurrence": "Invoices",
  "table": "Invoices",
  "recordId": 1,
  "fields": {
    "CustomerId": "C1",
    "Customer": "Acme Corp",
    "Amount": 1200,
    "Status": "Open",
    "Date": "2026-09-01",
    "Total": 1320
  },
  "empty": [
    "Attachment"
  ],
  "related": [
    {
      "occurrence": "Customers",
      "table": "Customers",
      "match": "Invoices::CustomerId = Customers::Id",
      "count": 1,
      "records": [
        {
          "recordId": 1,
          "fields": {
            "Id": "C1",
            "Name": "Acme Corp",
            "Email": "billing@acme.example"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "note": "Cite each fact as [Occurrence::Field] for this record, or [Occurrence::Field #recordId] for a related record. Only records and fields this account can see are here; secret-looking values are hidden. Related records list stored fields only."
}
```

<a id="create-record"></a>

### `create_record`

Create a record. Dates may be ISO (2026-10-11) or in the file's format.

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file whose privilege set may create records in the layout's table; a read-only API token can't.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `layout` | string | yes | Layout name; records are read and written through a layout |
| `fieldData` | object of string or number | yes | Field name -> value. Repetitions as "Field(2)". |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "create_record",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "fieldData": {
      "Customer": "Initech",
      "Amount": 99
    }
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "recordId": 4,
  "modId": 0
}
```

For an approval-gated AI agent account the write is not made: it is recorded for a person to approve, and the tool returns {"status": "pending_approval", "pendingId": …, "summary": …, "message": …} instead. Naming a masked field is refused ("cannot be modified"), whatever value is sent, the stand-in echoed back included.

<a id="update-record"></a>

### `update_record`

Change fields of a record, and its portal rows: portalData edits rows by recordId or adds rows without one; deleteRelated removes rows ("Portal.recordId"). Pass modId to fail if someone else changed it first. A record someone is editing is refused (error 301) until they are done.

**Hints:** idempotent

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file whose privilege set may edit the record (and its portal rows); a read-only API token can't.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `layout` | string | yes | Layout name; records are read and written through a layout |
| `recordId` | integer | yes | The record id, as find_records and get_record show it (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |
| `fieldData` | object of string or number | no | Field name -> value. Repetitions as "Field(2)". |
| `modId` | integer | no | The record's modId as last read; the change fails if someone has changed the record since (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |
| `portalData` | object of array of object of string or number | no | Portal name (or its table occurrence) -> rows: {"recordId": "12", "TO::Field": "new"} edits row 12; a row without recordId is added |
| `deleteRelated` | array of string | no | Portal rows to delete, as "Portal.recordId" |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "update_record",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "recordId": 1,
    "fieldData": {
      "Status": "Paid"
    }
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "modId": 1
}
```

For an approval-gated AI agent account the write is not made: it is recorded for a person to approve, and the tool returns {"status": "pending_approval", "pendingId": …, "summary": …, "message": …} instead. Portal edits are refused outright for such an agent. A masked field can't be changed: naming one is refused ("cannot be modified"), the stand-in echoed back included.

<a id="update-records"></a>

### `update_records`

Set the same fields on every record a find gives (up to 1,000), as this account, all or none: a record that cannot take the value (a rule, a lock, a privilege) stops the whole change. Run it with dryRun: true first to see each value that would change; expectCount refuses the change unless the find gives exactly that many records. Without a query it needs expectCount and changes every record. Only fields of the layout's own table. Every change is in the audit log, and the result's id undoes the batch with undo_data_fix. For different values per record, use update_record or a script.

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file; every change is made as this account, so its privilege set's edit rules apply, and only records it can view are touched. A read-only API token can't, and an approval-gated AI agent is refused.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `layout` | string | yes | Layout name; records are read and written through a layout |
| `query` | array of object of string or number or boolean | no | FileMaker find requests, as for find_records (at most 50 items) |
| `fieldData` | object of string or number or null | yes | Field -> new value (null empties the field) |
| `dryRun` | boolean | no | Say what would change, and change nothing |
| `expectCount` | integer | no | The number of records the find should give (min 0, max 9007199254740991) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "update_records",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "query": [
      {
        "Status": "Open",
        "Customer": "Initech"
      }
    ],
    "fieldData": {
      "Status": "Paid"
    },
    "expectCount": 2
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "id": "c21451e52878",
  "at": "2026-10-13T09:20:48.464Z",
  "layout": "Invoices",
  "summary": "2 of 2 records changed",
  "changes": 2,
  "matched": 2,
  "records": 2
}
```

With dryRun: true nothing is changed and the result is {dryRun: true, summary, matched, records, changes, total}: each value that would change (the first 200 in changes; total counts them all). Records that already have the value are matched but not counted in records. At most 1,000 records; a find that gives more, or not expectCount, changes nothing. A record that refuses the value (a validation rule, a lock, a privilege) stops the whole change.

<a id="upload-container"></a>

### `upload_container`

Put a file (image, PDF, anything) in a container field of a record, as Insert File does. Send it base64.

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file whose privilege set may edit the record and field; a read-only API token can't, and an approval-gated AI agent is refused. Files are limited to 100 MB.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `layout` | string | yes | Layout name; records are read and written through a layout |
| `recordId` | integer | yes | The record id, as find_records and get_record show it (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |
| `field` | string | yes | The container field's name |
| `repetition` | integer | no | Which repetition of the field, from 1 (default 1, min 1, max 9007199254740991) |
| `filename` | string | yes | The file's name, with its extension (at most 255 characters) |
| `mime` | string | no | The file's media type, e.g. application/pdf (default "application/octet-stream") |
| `data` | string | yes | The file, base64 |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "upload_container",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "recordId": 1,
    "field": "Attachment",
    "filename": "note.txt",
    "mime": "text/plain",
    "data": "aGVsbG8="
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "modId": 1
}
```

<a id="evaluate-calculation"></a>

### `evaluate_calculation`

Evaluate a FileMaker calculation formula in a layout's context, optionally on one record (fields, related fields through the relationship graph, custom functions, Get functions, ExecuteSQL). Use it to check a formula or compute a value without changing data.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Any identity whose privilege set can read every table and field (readsEverything), and the record if one is named; not available to scoped API tokens, so refused for an account with a masked field. Results that read a password, key or token field are hidden.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `layout` | string | yes | Layout name; records are read and written through a layout |
| `formula` | string | yes | FileMaker calculation syntax, e.g. Sum ( Line Items::Amount ) * 1.1 |
| `recordId` | integer | no | Record to evaluate on; omit for no record (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "evaluate_calculation",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "formula": "Amount * 2",
    "recordId": 1
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "value": "2400",
  "type": "number"
}
```

Without recordId, a formula that reads fields also gets a "note" that they read as empty.

<a id="delete-record"></a>

### `delete_record`

Delete a record. This cannot be undone.

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file whose privilege set may delete the record; a read-only API token can't.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `layout` | string | yes | Layout name; records are read and written through a layout |
| `recordId` | integer | yes | The record to delete (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "delete_record",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "recordId": 4
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "deleted": 4
}
```

For an approval-gated AI agent account the write is not made: it is recorded for a person to approve, and the tool returns {"status": "pending_approval", "pendingId": …, "summary": …, "message": …} instead.

<a id="revert-change"></a>

### `revert_change`

Put back what one entry of a record's audit log changed (the seq numbers come from explain_record_history, where each change carries its seq): an edit gets its old values again (fields picks some), a created record is deleted, a deleted record is made again under its id. It runs with this account's privileges, so it can put back only what the account could change by hand, and an agent whose changes need approval is held for approval. The put-back is logged as a change of its own that names the entry it reverts. Values that were not logged, containers and repetitions are left as they are and listed as skipped.

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file whose privilege set may make the change by hand (edit the fields, create or delete the record); a read-only API token can't. Refused while PII isolation is on.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `layout` | string | yes | Layout name; records are read and written through a layout |
| `recordId` | integer | yes | The record id, as find_records and get_record show it (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |
| `seq` | integer | yes | The audit entry to put back (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |
| `fields` | array of string | no | Only these fields of an edit; omit for all of them |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "revert_change",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "recordId": 1,
    "seq": 812,
    "fields": [
      "Status"
    ]
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "action": "updated",
  "fields": [
    "Status"
  ],
  "skipped": []
}
```

seq is the audit entry to put back (explain_record_history shows it on each change). action is updated, deleted (a created record is removed) or created (a deleted record is made again under its id). skipped lists fields left as they are: values that were not logged, containers, repetitions, and fields the account cannot see. The put-back is logged as a change of its own that names the entry it reverts. For an approval-gated AI agent account the write is not made: it is recorded for a person to approve, and the tool returns {"status": "pending_approval", "pendingId": …, "summary": …, "message": …} instead.

<a id="get-container"></a>

### `get_container`

Contents of a container field (image, PDF or file). Pass the value a record shows for the field (a download URL) or its container id. Images come back as images; text files as text; anything else as a summary.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file. A privilege set that can't read every table and field must pass the signed container URL from a record it can see; a bare container id is refused.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `container` | string or integer | yes | The container field's value from a record (a download URL), or its container id |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "get_container",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "container": 1
  }
}
```

Result:

```text
{"id":1,"filename":"note.txt","mime":"text/plain","bytes":5}

hello
```

Text files (up to 5 MB) come back as the JSON summary, a blank line and the text, as here. PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP images (up to 5 MB) come back as the JSON summary plus an image content item; anything else as JSON {id, filename, mime, bytes, note}.

<a id="sql-query"></a>

### `sql_query`

Run read-only SQL (SQLite dialect) for analysis across tables. Quote names with double quotes.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Any identity whose privilege set can read every table and field (readsEverything); not available to scoped API tokens. Values of password, key and token columns are hidden. An account with a masked field is refused, as it cannot read every field.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `sql` | string | yes | One SELECT statement in the SQLite dialect; quote table and field names with double quotes |
| `limit` | integer | no | Most rows to return (default 500, min 1, max 5000) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "sql_query",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "sql": "SELECT \"Customer\", SUM(\"Amount\") AS total FROM \"Invoices\" GROUP BY \"Customer\""
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
[
  {
    "Customer": "Acme Corp",
    "total": 1500
  },
  {
    "Customer": "Globex",
    "total": 450
  }
]
```

<a id="explain-solution"></a>

### `explain_solution`

A readable map of a solution: its tables (record counts, keys, layouts), relationships, script folders, which scripts buttons start, which are never called, the most called ones, and which reach outside (mail, network, plug-ins). Pass item (a table, layout, script, field, custom function or value list name) for that one in detail, with what calls or uses it.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access], or a set that can modify scripts and read everything (designAccess); not available to scoped API tokens.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `item` | string | no | A table, layout, script, field, custom function or value list name, for that one in detail (leave out for the whole map) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "explain_solution",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```text
# Invoices
Created with FileMaker Tabularius. 2 tables, 2 table occurrences, 1 relationships, 2 layouts, 1 scripts, 1 value lists, 0 custom functions, 1 accounts.

## Tables
- **Customers**: 2 records; 3 data, 0 calculation, 0 summary, 0 global fields; layouts: Customers
- **Invoices**: 3 records; 6 data, 1 calculation, 0 summary, 0 global fields; layouts: Invoices

## Relationships
- Invoices::CustomerId = Customers::Id

## Scripts
Not called by other scripts, buttons, triggers, custom menus or File Options (run from the Scripts menu, by URL or another file, or unused): Mark Paid.

## Value lists
- Status: Open, Paid

## Security
Privilege sets: [Full Access]. Accounts: Admin.
```

Markdown. With item, the text describes that one table, layout, script, field, custom function or value list.

<a id="solution-map"></a>

### `solution_map`

A cross-file map of a multi-file solution: which hosted files' table occurrences, value lists and scripts reach into which other files, plus any external references whose file is not hosted (a red reference in FileMaker). Use it to see how the files depend on one another before moving, renaming or removing one. Covers the files you can design; a file with AI turned off shows only as an opaque "AI off" node, with none of its names inside.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Any identity. Covers only the hosted files it may see the design of (designAccess in each); a file with AI turned off appears only as an opaque node.

**Parameters:** none

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "solution_map",
  "arguments": {}
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "files": [
    {
      "name": "Invoices",
      "reaches": [],
      "referencedBy": [
        "Invoices Staging"
      ],
      "unresolved": []
    },
    {
      "name": "Invoices Staging",
      "reaches": [
        "Invoices"
      ],
      "referencedBy": [],
      "unresolved": []
    }
  ],
  "references": [
    {
      "from": "Invoices Staging",
      "via": "occurrence",
      "item": "Live Customers",
      "file": "Invoices",
      "hosted": true,
      "detail": "base table Customers"
    }
  ],
  "unresolved": []
}
```

<a id="document-solution"></a>

### `document_solution`

Documentation of a solution as Markdown: every table with its fields (types, formulas, auto-enter, comments), the relationships, each layout (its table, fields, the scripts its buttons and triggers run) and each script (its own header comment, what starts it, what it calls, the layouts it goes to, whether it reaches outside). Pass section to get one part; whole solutions can be long.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access], or a set that can modify scripts and read everything (designAccess); not available to scoped API tokens.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `section` | "tables" \\| "relationships" \\| "layouts" \\| "scripts" \\| "custom functions" \\| "value lists" | no | Only this part of the documentation |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "document_solution",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "section": "scripts"
  }
}
```

Result:

```text
## Scripts

### Mark Paid

<a id="script-mark-paid"></a>

2 steps.

- Not started by any button, trigger or script (a menu, a schedule, or unused)
```

Markdown.

<a id="where-used"></a>

### `where_used`

Every place that uses a field ("Table::Field" or "Occurrence::Field"), script, layout, table, table occurrence, custom function or value list: calculations, auto-enter and validation, script steps, layout objects (fields, buttons, hide conditions, conditional formatting) and relationships. Use before renaming or deleting anything.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access], or a set that can modify scripts and read everything (designAccess); not available to scoped API tokens.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `name` | string | yes | The thing to look for: "Table::Field", a script, layout, table, table occurrence, custom function or value list |
| `kind` | "field" \\| "table" \\| "tableOccurrence" \\| "script" \\| "layout" \\| "customFunction" \\| "valueList" | no | What the name is, when it could be several things |
| `limit` | integer | no | Most places to list (default 200, min 1, max 1000) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "where_used",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "name": "Invoices::Status"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
[
  {
    "target": {
      "kind": "field",
      "name": "Invoices::Status"
    },
    "count": 2,
    "usages": [
      {
        "kind": "script",
        "where": "Script \"Mark Paid\", line 1",
        "text": "Set Field [ Invoices::Status ; \"Paid\" ]"
      },
      {
        "kind": "layout",
        "where": "Layout \"Invoices\"",
        "text": "field Invoices::Status"
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

<a id="search-solution"></a>

### `search_solution`

Search the whole design: table, field, layout, script, value list and custom function names, field comments, every formula, every script line and layout text. All words must appear. Use it to find where something is handled ("invoice email", "tax rate") or which field holds what a user means.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access], or a set that can modify scripts and read everything (designAccess); not available to scoped API tokens.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `text` | string | yes | The words to look for; all must appear |
| `limit` | integer | no | Most matches to return (default 100, min 1, max 1000) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "search_solution",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "text": "paid"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "count": 3,
  "byKind": {
    "script": 2,
    "valueList": 1
  },
  "hits": [
    {
      "kind": "script",
      "where": "Script \"Mark Paid\"",
      "text": "2 steps"
    },
    {
      "kind": "script",
      "where": "Script \"Mark Paid\", line 1",
      "text": "Set Field [ Invoices::Status ; \"Paid\" ]"
    },
    {
      "kind": "valueList",
      "where": "Value list \"Status\"",
      "text": "Open, Paid"
    }
  ]
}
```

### `describe_layout`

Fields on a layout, as find_records names them, with type, value list values, how many records have a value, ranges (numbers, dates) and the common or example values, related and portal fields included (find_records searches them as Occurrence::Field); plus its portals.
