```json
    {
      "name": "Attachment",
      "type": "container",
      "kind": "data"
    },
    {
      "name": "Total",
      "type": "number",
      "kind": "calculation",
      "filled": 3,
      "distinct": 3,
      "min": 330,
      "max": 1320,
      "examples": [
        1320,
        330,
        495
      ]
    }
  ],
  "portals": [],
  "findSyntax": "Each find request is {field: criteria}; fields in one request are ANDed, requests are ORed, {\"omit\": true} in a request excludes its matches. Criteria: \"abc\" finds a word starting abc; \"=abc\" a whole word; \"==abc\" the whole field; \"=\" empty; \"*\" any value; \"<100\", \">=5\", \"1...10\" ranges; dates as 2026-01-31 or in the file's own format, \"2026-01-01...2026-03-31\" for a range; * (any text) and @ (one character) wildcards; \"quoted phrase\". Related fields are searched as \"Occurrence::Field\": a record matches when one of its related records matches all the criteria on that occurrence (\"customers with an unpaid invoice over 500\")."
}
```

<a id="check-calculation"></a>

### `check_calculation`

Check a drafted FileMaker formula in a layout's context without changing data: syntax errors with FileMaker's error code, unknown fields, table occurrences and functions (with "did you mean"), wrong parameter counts, and the result on the first few records.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the layout and whose privilege set can read every table and field (readsEverything); not available to scoped API tokens.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `layout` | string | yes | Layout name; records are read and written through a layout |
| `formula` | string | yes | The formula to check, as typed in Specify Calculation |
| `sampleRecords` | integer | no | Evaluate on this many records of the layout (default 3, min 0, max 20) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "check_calculation",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "formula": "Amout * 1.2",
    "sampleRecords": 2
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "Amout",
      "found": false
    }
  ],
  "functions": [],
  "problems": [
    "\"Amout\" is not a field of Invoices, a Let variable or a function (did you mean \"Amount\"?)"
  ],
  "variables": [],
  "results": [
    {
      "recordId": 1,
      "error": "The field \"Amout\" cannot be found"
    },
    {
      "recordId": 2,
      "error": "The field \"Amout\" cannot be found"
    }
  ]
}
```

A formula that checks out has ok: true and results like {"recordId": 1, "value": "1440", "type": "number"}.

<a id="explain-value"></a>

### `explain_value`

Why a field holds the value it does on a record: its formula (calculation or auto-enter), the value of every field it reads, each step of the evaluation with its intermediate result, whether "Do not evaluate if all referenced fields are empty" kept it empty, whether the stored value still matches the formula, the chain of calculations behind it, and lint warnings. Read-only.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access], or a set that can modify scripts and read everything (designAccess); not available to scoped API tokens. Values of password, key and token fields are hidden. The function checks the privilege set itself: a field the set can't see is refused (the error says the privilege set can't see Table::Field), and a field the formula reads that the set can't see comes back as {field, type, kind, hidden: true} with no value, its dependencies shown without formulas.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `layout` | string | yes | Layout name; records are read and written through a layout |
| `field` | string | yes | A field of the layout's table |
| `recordId` | integer | no | Record to explain it on; omit for globals or to see the formula alone (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "explain_value",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "field": "Total",
    "recordId": 1
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "table": "Invoices",
  "field": "Total",
  "type": "number",
  "kind": "calculation",
  "storage": "stored",
  "value": "1320",
  "formula": "Amount * 1.1",
  "context": "Invoices",
  "doNotEvaluateIfEmpty": true,
  "warnings": [],
  "references": [
    {
      "field": "Amount",
      "type": "number",
      "kind": "normal",
      "value": "1200",
      "empty": false
    }
  ],
  "result": "1320",
  "steps": {
    "expr": "Amount * 1.1",
    "value": "1320",
    "type": "number",
    "steps": [
      {
        "expr": "Amount",
        "value": "1200",
        "type": "number"
      }
    ]
  },
  "matchesStored": true
}
```

<a id="check-record"></a>

### `check_record`

Why does this record look wrong? Checks every calculation and validated field on one record as it is now: a formula that fails, a stored value that is no longer what its formula gives, a result left empty by an empty input, a reference to a field that isn't there, a value its validation would refuse, and formula warnings that change a result. Each problem lists the values its formula read and, in causedBy, the fields on the record it reads that have problems of their own, so start there; root causes come first. Then explain_value on one field shows each step. Read-only.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access], or a set that can modify scripts and read everything (designAccess), and that may view the record; not available to scoped API tokens. Values of password, key and token fields are hidden. A calculation the privilege set can't see is skipped (not counted in checked), and an input it reads that the set can't see has hidden: true and no value.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `layout` | string | yes | Layout name; records are read and written through a layout |
| `recordId` | integer | yes | The record to check (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "check_record",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "recordId": 1
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "table": "Invoices",
  "checked": 2,
  "problems": [
    {
      "field": "Amount",
      "kind": "validation",
      "value": "150000",
      "message": "Amount wouldn't pass its validation now: Field \"Amount\" must be between 0 and 100000."
    },
    {
      "field": "Total",
      "value": "999",
      "formula": "Amount * 1.1",
      "inputs": [
        {
          "field": "Amount",
          "value": "150000"
        }
      ],
      "now": "165000",
      "kind": "stale",
      "message": "Total shows a value its formula no longer gives: the stored value was worked out when the record last changed, and something it reads has changed since.",
      "causedBy": [
        "Amount"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

checked counts the calculations and validated fields looked at. Problems come root causes first: a problem's causedBy names fields on the record that have problems of their own, so start there. kind is one of error, missing-reference, validation, stale, empty-input, not-evaluated or warning.

<a id="explain-related"></a>

### `explain_related`

Why a portal or related field on a record shows what it does (or nothing): the relationship path followed, each match field with its values on both sides and how many records each finds on its own, the portal's filter and sort, every related record with whether it is shown and why, and a one-line verdict ("empty because Customers::Id is empty on this record"). Pass candidate to ask why a particular record of the far table is or isn't there: each match is checked against it and the portal filter is evaluated step by step. Read-only.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Any identity whose privilege set can read every table and field (readsEverything) and view the record; not available to scoped API tokens. Values of password, key and token fields are hidden.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `layout` | string | yes | Layout name; records are read and written through a layout |
| `recordId` | integer | yes | The record the portal or related field is on (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |
| `portal` | string | no | Portal name (or its table occurrence) on the layout |
| `field` | string | no | A related field, TableOccurrence::Field, instead of a portal |
| `candidate` | integer | no | Record id in the far table to explain being in or out (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |
| `limit` | integer | no | Related records to list (default 25) (min 1, max 200) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "explain_related",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "recordId": 1,
    "field": "Customers::Name"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "kind": "related field",
  "from": {
    "occurrence": "Invoices",
    "table": "Invoices",
    "recordId": 1
  },
  "to": {
    "occurrence": "Customers",
    "table": "Customers"
  },
  "path": [
    {
      "relationship": "Invoices::CustomerId = Customers::Id",
      "from": "Invoices",
      "to": "Customers",
      "match": [
        {
          "match": "Invoices::CustomerId = Customers::Id",
          "values": [
            "C1"
          ],
          "matches": 1
        }
      ],
      "records": 1
    }
  ],
  "related": 1,
  "rows": [
    {
      "recordId": 1,
      "shown": true,
      "keys": {
        "Customers::Id": "C1"
      },
      "reason": "Shown: its match fields match this record"
    }
  ],
  "verdict": "Customers::Name shows record 1, the first of 1 related record: \"Acme Corp\"",
  "notes": [],
  "field": {
    "name": "Customers::Name",
    "recordId": 1,
    "value": "Acme Corp"
  }
}
```

<a id="lint-formulas"></a>

### `lint_formulas`

Warnings for every calculation and auto-enter formula in a file (or one table): text fields in arithmetic, dates compared with text, "Do not evaluate if all referenced fields are empty" hiding the result the formula was written for (IsEmpty flags, defaults) or not applying (formulas reading containers), stored calculations reading globals or related records, unused Let variables, missing fields. FileMaker accepts all of these silently.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access], or a set that can modify scripts and read everything (designAccess); not available to scoped API tokens.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `table` | string | no | Only this table's fields |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "lint_formulas",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "table": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "fieldsWithWarnings": 1,
  "fields": [
    {
      "field": "Invoices::Label",
      "warnings": [
        "type-mix: Customer + 1 does arithmetic on the text field Customer: FileMaker uses only the digits in it, so \"12 boxes\" counts as 12 and \"N/A\" as nothing.",
        "empty-rule: When every field it reads is empty, the formula gives \"1\", but \"Do not evaluate if all referenced fields are empty\" is on, so the field stays empty instead. Turn the option off if that value is wanted (typical for IsEmpty, flags and defaults)."
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

At most 200 fields are listed; a "note" says how many more there are.

<a id="check-script"></a>

### `check_script`

Check a drafted script without running it. Write it as FileMaker's script workspace shows steps, one per line (as get_script returns them): Set Field [ Invoices::Status ; "Paid" ], Perform Script [ "Name" ; Parameter: ... ]. Reports unknown steps, unbalanced If/Loop, missing layouts, scripts, table occurrences and fields (with "did you mean"), calculation or summary fields being set, every formula's problems, $variables read before they are set, and steps that reach outside the solution.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access], or a set that can modify scripts and read everything (designAccess); not available to scoped API tokens.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `script` | string | yes | Script text, one step per line |
| `layout` | string | no | Layout the script starts on (context for its formulas); default the first layout |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "check_script",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "script": "Set Field [ Invoices::Stauts ; \"Paid\" ]",
    "layout": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "steps": 1,
  "problems": [
    {
      "line": 1,
      "step": "Set Field",
      "message": "\"Invoices\" has no field named \"Stauts\""
    }
  ],
  "warnings": [],
  "layouts": [],
  "scripts": [],
  "fields": []
}
```

<a id="search-records"></a>

### `search_records`

Search the text of every record, in every table, for words, best matches first, like a site search: "acme march invoice" finds records whose text fields hold those words, in any field. Words match by prefix, ignoring case and accents. Use it when the request doesn't say which table or field to look in; use find_records for exact criteria (ranges, dates, one field). Each hit has the table, record id, the fields that matched, and a layout for get_record.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file. Only records and fields its privilege set can see are searched; a masked field is not.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `text` | string | yes | Words to look for |
| `tables` | array of string | no | Only these tables (at most 200 items) |
| `limit` | integer | no | Most records to return (default 25, min 1, max 200) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "search_records",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "text": "acme",
    "limit": 2
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "query": "acme",
  "matchedAll": true,
  "hits": [
    {
      "table": "Customers",
      "recordId": 1,
      "score": 100,
      "matches": [
        {
          "field": "Name",
          "text": "[Acme] Corp"
        },
        {
          "field": "Email",
          "text": "billing@[acme].example"
        }
      ],
      "layout": "Customers"
    },
    {
      "table": "Invoices",
      "recordId": 1,
      "score": 95,
      "matches": [
        {
          "field": "Customer",
          "text": "[Acme] Corp"
        }
      ],
      "layout": "Invoices"
    }
  ]
}
```

When the file uses tables of files that aren't hosted (and tables isn't given), the result also has "notSearched" naming them.

<a id="semantic-find"></a>

### `semantic_find`

Find records by meaning, best matches first: "customers unhappy about late delivery" finds records whose stored embedding is closest to the question, even with none of those words. Needs a field holding embeddings (a container field filled by Insert Embedding, or text holding a vector as a JSON array) on the layout, made with the same embedding model this server uses; use search_records for words and find_records for exact criteria. Each match has the record id and its similarity (-1 to 1); read the records with get_record on the same layout. The question text goes to the server's embedding model.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file, on a server started with an embedding model (--ai-embed-url): without one the tool is not offered. Only records its privilege set can view are compared, and the vector field must be readable (not hidden or masked). Refused while personal data isolation is on. Not available if the file's AI switch is off.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `layout` | string | yes | Layout that shows the records and the embedding field |
| `field` | string | yes | The field holding each record's embedding |
| `text` | string | yes | What to look for, in words (at most 8000 characters) |
| `limit` | integer | no | Most results to return (default 10, min 1, max 100) |
| `threshold` | number | no | Leave out matches less similar than this (min -1, max 1) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "semantic_find",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Support",
    "layout": "Tickets",
    "field": "Embedding",
    "text": "delivery was late",
    "limit": 2
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "layout": "Tickets",
  "field": "Embedding",
  "matches": [
    {
      "recordId": 14,
      "similarity": 0.912345
    },
    {
      "recordId": 3,
      "similarity": 0.87021
    }
  ],
  "scored": 120,
  "noEmbedding": 2,
  "differentLength": 0
}
```

The question is sent to the server's embedding model (a hosted endpoint, if that is what --ai-embed-url names). The field holds vectors Insert Embedding made (a container) or text holding a vector as a JSON array, from the same model. At most 50,000 records are compared and a scan stops after 10 seconds: "incomplete" says so. Vectors of another length than the model's are an error when none can be compared, otherwise counted in "differentLength". Read the records with get_record on the same layout. A vector reveals some of its source field's meaning: give the embedding field the access of the field it was made from. The question counts against the daily and monthly AI limits (at most 8,000 characters).

<a id="summarize-records"></a>

### `summarize_records`

Totals of a found set, overall or broken down by up to 3 fields, like a sub-summary report: count of records, and sum, average, min, max, count or distinct count of fields. "Open invoices per customer with their total" is query [{"Status":"Open"}], groupBy ["Customer"], measures [{"field":"Amount","fn":"sum"}]. Use it instead of reading every record with find_records. Groups come largest first.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file. The find and the totals cover only the records and fields its privilege set can see; grouping or measuring a masked field is an error.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `layout` | string | yes | Layout name; records are read and written through a layout |
| `query` | array of object of string or number or boolean | no | Find requests, as find_records takes them; omit for all records (at most 50 items) |
| `groupBy` | array of string | no | Up to 3 fields to break the totals down by (omit for one overall total) (at most 3 items) |
| `by` | "day" \\| "week" \\| "month" \\| "quarter" \\| "year" | no | Group date and timestamp fields in groupBy by this period ("2026-07" for month), in date order: "leads per month" |
| `measures` | array of object | no | What to work out for each group: a field and count, sum, average, min, max or distinct (count of different values) (at most 10 items) |
| `measures[].field` | string | yes |  |
| `measures[].fn` | "count" \\| "sum" \\| "average" \\| "min" \\| "max" \\| "distinct" | yes |  |
| `limit` | integer | no | Groups to return (default 50, min 1, max 500) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "summarize_records",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "groupBy": [
      "Customer"
    ],
    "measures": [
      {
        "field": "Amount",
        "fn": "sum"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "layout": "Invoices",
  "foundCount": 3,
  "totals": {
    "sum(Amount)": 1950
  },
  "groups": [
    {
      "values": {
        "Customer": "Acme Corp"
      },
      "count": 2,
      "measures": {
        "sum(Amount)": 1500
      }
    },
    {
      "values": {
        "Customer": "Globex"
      },
      "count": 1,
      "measures": {
        "sum(Amount)": 450
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<a id="list-dashboards"></a>

### `list_dashboards`

Dashboards saved in a file: charts, summary tables and numbers worked out live from finds. get_dashboard shows one with its numbers.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file. Every dashboard saved in the file is listed.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "list_dashboards",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "dashboards": [
    {
      "id": "75b887eb757a",
      "name": "Sales",
      "description": "Invoice totals",
      "widgets": 1,
      "account": "Admin",
      "updated": "2026-10-13T09:15:02.450Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

<a id="get-dashboard"></a>

### `get_dashboard`

A saved dashboard (by id or name) with each widget worked out now, as this account: its find in words (relative dates with the range they mean today), its grouping, and its numbers.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file. Each widget is worked out as this account, from the records and fields its privilege set can see.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `dashboard` | string | yes | Its id or name |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "get_dashboard",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "dashboard": "Sales"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "dashboard": {
    "id": "75b887eb757a",
    "name": "Sales",
    "description": "Invoice totals",
    "widgets": [
      {
        "title": "Revenue by customer",
        "kind": "chart",
        "chart": "bar",
        "layout": "Invoices",
        "groupBy": [
          "Customer"
        ],
        "measure": {
          "field": "Amount",
          "fn": "sum"
        }
      }
    ],
    "account": "Admin",
    "created": "2026-10-13T09:15:02.450Z",
    "updated": "2026-10-13T09:15:02.450Z"
  },
  "data": [
    {
      "title": "Revenue by customer",
      "kind": "chart",
      "chart": "bar",
      "layout": "Invoices",
      "find": [
        "All records"
      ],
      "grouping": "Sum of Amount by Customer",
      "foundCount": 3,
      "xTitle": "Customer",
      "yTitle": "sum(Amount)",
      "categories": [
        "Acme Corp",
        "Globex"
      ],
      "series": [
        {
          "name": "sum(Amount)",
          "values": [
            1500,
            450
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<a id="save-dashboard"></a>

### `save_dashboard`

Save a dashboard in a file from a plain-English request: "revenue by month for my top 10 customers this year" is a line chart on an Invoices layout, query [{"Date": "this year"}], groupBy ["Date", "Customer"], by "month", measure sum of Amount, top {field: "Customer", n: 10}, plus a table of the same grouped by Customer. Call describe_layout first for field names. preview: true works it out without saving, to check the numbers. Saving over an existing dashboard (same name) needs replace: true.

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file; numbers are worked out as this account. Replacing an existing dashboard needs the account that made it, [Full Access], or the server administrator.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `name` | string | yes | The dashboard's name |
| `description` | string | no | What the dashboard shows, for people reading the list |
| `widgets` | array of object | yes | The charts, tables and numbers, up to 24 (at least 1 items, at most 24 items) |
| `widgets[].title` | string | yes |  |
| `widgets[].kind` | "chart" \\| "table" \\| "number" | yes | A chart, a summary table (one row per group), or one number |
| `widgets[].chart` | "column" \\| "bar" \\| "line" \\| "pie" | no | For a chart; line keeps dates and periods in order |
| `widgets[].layout` | string | yes | Layout name; records are read and written through a layout |
| `widgets[].query` | array of object of string or number or boolean | no | Find requests, as find_records takes them; omit for all records. Date and timestamp criteria may be relative and stay so: "today", "this week", "this month", "last month", "this quarter", "this year", "last year", "year to date", "last 30 days" (at most 50 items) |
| `widgets[].groupBy` | array of string | no | A chart: the categories, then optionally a field whose values become separate series (2 at most). A table: up to 3 (at most 3 items) |
| `widgets[].by` | "day" \\| "week" \\| "month" \\| "quarter" \\| "year" | no | Group date and timestamp fields in groupBy by this period |
| `widgets[].measure` | object | no | Omit to count records |
| `widgets[].measure.field` | string | yes |  |
| `widgets[].measure.fn` | "count" \\| "sum" \\| "average" \\| "min" \\| "max" \\| "distinct" | yes |  |
| `widgets[].top` | object | no | Only records whose value of this field is among the n largest by the measure: "my top 10 customers" is {field: "Customer", n: 10} |
| `widgets[].top.field` | string | yes |  |
| `widgets[].top.n` | integer | yes | (min 1, max 50) |
| `widgets[].limit` | integer | no | Groups to show (default 12 for a chart, 50 for a table) (min 1, max 200) |
| `preview` | boolean | no | true works the numbers out and saves nothing |
| `replace` | boolean | no | true to save over a dashboard with the same name |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "save_dashboard",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "name": "Sales",
    "widgets": [
      {
        "title": "Revenue by customer",
        "kind": "table",
        "layout": "Invoices",
        "groupBy": [
          "Customer"
        ],
        "measure": {
          "field": "Amount",
          "fn": "sum"
        }
      }
    ],
    "preview": true
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "preview": true,
  "name": "Sales",
  "widgets": [
    {
      "title": "Revenue by customer",
      "kind": "table",
      "layout": "Invoices",
      "groupBy": [
        "Customer"
      ],
      "measure": {
        "field": "Amount",
        "fn": "sum"
      }
    }
  ],
  "data": [
    {
      "title": "Revenue by customer",
      "kind": "table",
      "layout": "Invoices",
      "find": [
        "All records"
      ],
      "grouping": "Sum of Amount by Customer",
      "foundCount": 3,
      "columns": [
        "Customer",
        "sum(Amount)",
        "Records"
      ],
      "rows": [
        [
          "Acme Corp",
          1500,
          2
        ],
        [
          "Globex",
          450,
          1
        ]
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Without preview the dashboard is saved and the result is {"saved": true, "dashboard": {…}, "url": "/app/dashboard.html?db=…&id=…", "data": […]}.

<a id="find-data-problems"></a>

### `find_data_problems`

Data cleanup, step one (changes nothing): likely duplicate records on a layout (the same email or phone, names nearly alike with the same address), values not in the field's value list ("Actve" for "Active"), and malformed phone numbers and email addresses, each with a suggested fix where there is a likely one. Show the person what was found; fix_data_problems applies what they pick.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file. Only the records it can view and the text and number fields it can see are scanned. Changes nothing.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `layout` | string | yes | Layout name; records are read and written through a layout |
| `checks` | array of "duplicates" \\| "valueLists" \\| "consistency" \\| "phones" \\| "emails" | no | Which checks (default all) |
| `fields` | array of string | no | Only these fields of the layout's table |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "find_data_problems",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Customers",
    "checks": [
      "emails"
    ]
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "layout": "Customers",
  "table": "Customers",
  "scanned": 2,
  "compared": [],
  "duplicates": [],
  "fixes": [
    {
      "check": "emails",
      "field": "Email",
      "from": "ap@globex",
      "reason": "not a valid email address",
      "count": 1,
      "recordIds": [
        2
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<a id="fix-data-problems"></a>

### `fix_data_problems`

Data cleanup, step two: apply fixes ({field, from, to}: every record with that value gets the new one) and merges ({keep, remove: [ids], fill?}: the kept record gets fill for its empty fields, related records move to it, the others are deleted), from find_data_problems, all or none, as this account. Only what the person chose. Every change is in the audit log, and the result's id undoes the whole batch with undo_data_fix. dryRun: true says what would change (each value, each record deleted) and changes nothing.

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file; every change is made as this account, so its privilege set's edit and delete rules apply, and only records it can view are touched.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `layout` | string | yes | Layout name; records are read and written through a layout |
| `dryRun` | boolean | no | Work out what would change, and change nothing |
| `fixes` | array of object | no | Values to change: {field, from, to} gives every record with that value the new one (at most 200 items) |
| `fixes[].field` | string | yes |  |
| `fixes[].from` | string | yes |  |
| `fixes[].to` | string | yes |  |
| `merges` | array of object | no | Duplicates to merge: {keep, remove: [record ids], fill?} keeps one record and moves the others' related records to it (at most 200 items) |
| `merges[].keep` | integer | yes | (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |
| `merges[].remove` | array of integer | yes | (at least 1 items) |
| `merges[].fill` | object of string or number or null | no |  |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "fix_data_problems",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "fixes": [
      {
        "field": "Status",
        "from": "Actve",
        "to": "Active"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "id": "c21451e52878",
  "at": "2026-10-13T09:20:48.464Z",
  "layout": "Invoices",
  "summary": "1 value fixed",
  "changes": 1,
  "fixed": 1,
  "merged": 0
}
```

With dryRun: true nothing is changed and the result is {dryRun: true, summary, fixed, merged, changes, total}: each value that would change and each record that would be deleted (the first 200 in changes; total counts them all).

<a id="plan-import"></a>

### `plan_import`

Importing a spreadsheet, step one: match a CSV's columns to a layout's fields (by name and by what the values look like), with the fixes each column needs (date order, currency and thousands separators, yes/no, value list spellings, Excel dates, phone numbers, a full name or "City, ST 12345" split across several fields), a preview of what rows become with any problems, and rows that repeat a record already in the table or an earlier row (by keys: an email, an id or code). Check the matching, change columns, transforms or keys if needed (pass them back to see the new preview), then import_records.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file. Only fields on the layout its privilege set can modify are offered (no calculations, summaries or containers). Changes nothing.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `layout` | string | yes | Layout name; records are read and written through a layout |
| `data` | string | yes | The file's contents: comma-, tab-, semicolon- or pipe-separated text |
| `format` | "csv" \\| "tab" \\| "semicolon" \\| "pipe" | no | csv, tab, semicolon or pipe (worked out from the first line when left out) |
| `headerRow` | boolean | no | Whether the first row holds column names (worked out when left out) |
| `columns` | array of object | no | For each column (0-based), the field it goes into (null: not imported) and its fixes. A column can be listed more than once to split it, each entry with one part fix: name-first, name-middle, name-last (a full name) or city, state, postcode ("Springfield, IL 62704") |
| `columns[].column` | integer | yes | (min 0, max 9007199254740991) |
| `columns[].field` | string or null | yes |  |
| `columns[].transforms` | array of "trim" \\| "number" \\| "date-mdy" \\| "date-dmy" \\| "date-ymd" \\| "excel-date" \\| "time" \\| "yes-no" \\| "value-list" \\| "upper" \\| "lower" \\| "title-case" \\| "digits" \\| "phone" \\| "name-first" \\| "name-middle" \\| "name-last" \\| "city" \\| "state" \\| "postcode" | no |  |
| `keys` | array of string | no | Fields that tell records apart, to find duplicates |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "plan_import",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Customers",
    "data": "Name,Email\nInitech,info@initech.example\nAcme Corp,billing@acme.example\n"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "layout": "Customers",
  "table": "Customers",
  "rows": 2,
  "headerRow": true,
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "Id",
      "type": "text"
    },
    {
      "name": "Name",
      "type": "text"
    },
    {
      "name": "Email",
      "type": "text"
    }
  ],
  "columns": [
    {
      "column": 0,
      "header": "Name",
      "field": "Name",
      "transforms": [],
      "sample": [
        "Initech",
        "Acme Corp"
      ],
      "by": "name",
      "why": "same name"
    },
    {
      "column": 1,
      "header": "Email",
      "field": "Email",
      "transforms": [],
      "sample": [
        "info@initech.example",
        "billing@acme.example"
      ],
      "by": "name",
      "why": "same name"
    }
  ],
  "keys": [
    "Email"
  ],
  "preview": [
    {
      "row": 2,
      "values": {
        "Name": "Initech",
        "Email": "info@initech.example"
      },
      "issues": []
    },
    {
      "row": 3,
      "values": {
        "Name": "Acme Corp",
        "Email": "billing@acme.example"
      },
      "issues": [],
      "duplicate": {
        "of": "existing",
        "recordId": 1
      }
    }
  ],
  "summary": {
    "ready": 1,
    "withIssues": 0,
    "duplicatesInFile": 0,
    "duplicatesExisting": 1
  }
}
```

<a id="import-records"></a>

### `import_records`

Importing a spreadsheet, step two: each row becomes a new record of the layout's table, as this account, with the columns, fixes and keys from plan_import. skipDuplicates leaves out rows that repeat a record or an earlier row; skipIssues leaves out rows with a value that couldn't be fixed. Only after the person agreed to the plan. The whole import is one step: undo_import with the result's id deletes the records it made (except ones changed since).

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file; records are created as this account, so its privilege set must allow creating records in the layout's table, and only fields it can modify are filled.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `layout` | string | yes | Layout name; records are read and written through a layout |
| `data` | string | yes | The file's contents: comma-, tab-, semicolon- or pipe-separated text |
| `format` | "csv" \\| "tab" \\| "semicolon" \\| "pipe" | no | csv, tab, semicolon or pipe (worked out from the first line when left out) |
| `headerRow` | boolean | yes | Whether the first row holds column names rather than data |
| `columns` | array of object | yes | For each column (0-based), the field it goes into (null: not imported) and its fixes. A column can be listed more than once to split it, each entry with one part fix: name-first, name-middle, name-last (a full name) or city, state, postcode ("Springfield, IL 62704") |
| `columns[].column` | integer | yes | (min 0, max 9007199254740991) |
| `columns[].field` | string or null | yes |  |
| `columns[].transforms` | array of "trim" \\| "number" \\| "date-mdy" \\| "date-dmy" \\| "date-ymd" \\| "excel-date" \\| "time" \\| "yes-no" \\| "value-list" \\| "upper" \\| "lower" \\| "title-case" \\| "digits" \\| "phone" \\| "name-first" \\| "name-middle" \\| "name-last" \\| "city" \\| "state" \\| "postcode" | no |  |
| `keys` | array of string | no | Fields that identify a record (an email, an id), to spot rows that repeat one |
| `skipDuplicates` | boolean | no | Leave out rows that repeat a record already there or an earlier row |
| `skipIssues` | boolean | no | Leave out rows with a value that could not be fixed |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "import_records",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Customers",
    "data": "Name,Email\nInitech,info@initech.example\nAcme Corp,billing@acme.example\n",
    "headerRow": true,
    "columns": [
      {
        "column": 0,
        "field": "Name"
      },
      {
        "column": 1,
        "field": "Email"
      }
    ],
    "keys": [
      "Email"
    ],
    "skipDuplicates": true
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "id": "1267b43bbfc1",
  "foundSet": [
    3
  ],
  "imported": 1,
  "skipped": [
    {
      "row": 3,
      "why": "same as record 1"
    }
  ]
}
```

<a id="undo-import"></a>

### `undo_import`

Takes back an import from import_records (or the web client): deletes the records it made, except ones changed since. Without id, lists the recent imports.

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file can list the recent imports. Undoing one needs the account that made it, [Full Access], or the server administrator; records are deleted as this account.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `id` | string | no | The import's id from import_records; leave out to list recent imports |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "undo_import",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "id": "1267b43bbfc1"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "deleted": 1,
  "kept": []
}
```

Without id the result is the recent imports: [{"id", "at", "account", "layout", "file", "imported"}, …].

<a id="undo-data-fix"></a>

### `undo_data_fix`

Undo a batch fix_data_problems applied (by its id), all or none: values set back and merged records put back. Fields changed again since are left alone and listed. Without id, lists the batches applied.

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** Any identity that can use the file; values are set back and records restored as this account, with its privileges.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `id` | string | no | The batch id from fix_data_problems; leave out to list the batches |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "undo_data_fix",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "id": "c21451e52878"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "undone": 1,
  "skipped": []
}
```

Without id the result is {"history": [{"id", "at", "account", "layout", "summary", "changes"}, …]}.

<a id="find-stale-calcs"></a>

### `find_stale_calcs`

Stored calculations whose saved value is no longer what the formula gives now, with counts per field (changes nothing). FileMaker recomputes a stored calculation only when its own record changes, so one that reads other records (ExecuteSQL) or names fields at run time (Evaluate, GetField) falls behind; a converted file keeps FileMaker's stored values until someone refreshes them. A "this record only" field that differs points at a formula Tabularius works out differently, so say so rather than suggest refreshing it. refresh_stale_calcs brings chosen fields up to date.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Any identity whose privilege set can read every table and field (readsEverything); not available to scoped API tokens. Changes nothing.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `table` | string | no | Only this table |
| `fields` | array of string | no | Only these fields |
| `limit` | integer | no | Records looked at per table (default 10,000) (max 9007199254740991) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "find_stale_calcs",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "fields": [
    {
      "table": "Invoices",
      "field": "Total",
      "cause": "this record only",
      "records": 3,
      "looked": 3,
      "stale": 1,
      "wasEmpty": 0,
      "nowEmpty": 0,
      "failing": 0,
      "recordIds": [
        2
      ],
      "examples": [
        {
          "recordId": 2,
          "stored": 999,
          "now": 330
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "skipped": [],
  "looked": 3,
  "stale": 1,
  "note": "Nothing was changed. \"other records\" and \"fields named at run time\" are expected to drift in FileMaker too; refresh_stale_calcs brings chosen ones up to date and can be undone. \"this record only\" fields FileMaker keeps current, so a difference there more likely means Tabularius works the formula out differently: check before refreshing."
}
```

<a id="refresh-stale-calcs"></a>

### `refresh_stale_calcs`

Bring chosen stored calculations up to date (from find_stale_calcs): every record, or the ones listed, whose stored value differs from what the formula gives now gets the new value, all or none. Only what the person chose. Records where the formula fails are left alone, and modification timestamps don't change. Every change is in the audit log; the result's id undoes the batch with undo_stale_refresh. Needs [Full Access].

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** [Full Access] or the server administrator.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `fields` | array of object | yes | The stored calculations to bring up to date, each {table, field, recordIds?} (all records when recordIds is left out) (at least 1 items) |
| `fields[].table` | string | yes |  |
| `fields[].field` | string | yes |  |
| `fields[].recordIds` | array of integer | no |  |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "refresh_stale_calcs",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "fields": [
      {
        "table": "Invoices",
        "field": "Total"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "id": "2ae18f09ced7",
  "at": "2026-10-13T09:30:00.078Z",
  "summary": "1 stored value brought up to date in Invoices::Total",
  "changes": 1,
  "perField": [
    {
      "table": "Invoices",
      "field": "Total",
      "refreshed": 1,
      "failing": 0,
      "skipped": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

<a id="undo-stale-refresh"></a>

### `undo_stale_refresh`

Undo a batch refresh_stale_calcs made (by its id): the stored values it replaced are put back, except where they changed again since. Without id, lists the refreshes made.

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** [Full Access] or the server administrator, also to list the refreshes.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `id` | string | no | The refresh's id from refresh_stale_calcs; leave out to list the refreshes |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "undo_stale_refresh",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "id": "2ae18f09ced7"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "undone": 1,
  "skipped": 0
}
```

Without id the result is {"history": [{"id", "at", "account", "summary", "changes"}, …]}.

<a id="list-automations"></a>

### `list_automations`

Automations in a file: what sets each off (records created or changed, a field changed, a condition) and the script it runs on the record, with its recent runs.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] or the server administrator.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "list_automations",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "automations": [
    {
      "name": "Paid date",
      "enabled": true,
      "layout": "Invoices",
      "on": "update",
      "fields": [
        "Status"
      ],
      "condition": "Status = \"Paid\"",
      "script": "Mark Paid",
      "account": "Admin",
      "id": "841a547c2332",
      "created": "2026-10-13T09:40:13.859Z",
      "updated": "2026-10-13T09:40:13.859Z",
      "createdBy": "Admin",
      "trigger": "When a record in Invoices is changed, and the change is to Status, if Status = \"Paid\": run \"Mark Paid\" on that record (from layout Invoices) as Admin",
      "runs": []
    }
  ]
}
```

<a id="try-automation"></a>

### `try_automation`

Automations in plain English, step one: "when an invoice is marked paid, set the paid date and add a note to the customer" is on "update", fields ["Status"], condition Status = "Paid", and a script that sets PaidDate and creates the note. This checks it and runs it once on a throwaway copy of the file, offline: test gives the change that sets it off ({"Status": "Paid"}), made on a record where the condition is false first. Returns what the script would change. Nothing changes in the file; save_automation turns it on.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] or the server administrator. Runs once on a throwaway copy of the file, offline; nothing changes in the file.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `name` | string | yes | The automation's name |
| `description` | string | no | What it does, in a sentence |
| `layout` | string | yes | Its table's records are watched; the script runs from this layout on the record |
| `on` | "create" \\| "update" \\| "createOrUpdate" \\| "delete" | yes | What sets it off; delete: the script gets the deleted record as JSON in Get ( ScriptParameter ), with no fields, condition or parameter |
| `fields` | array of string | no | update: only when one of these fields changed ("when Status changes") |
| `condition` | string | no | FileMaker formula on the record after the change; runs only when true (Status = "Paid") |
| `script` | string | no | An existing script to run; or give scriptText |
| `scriptText` | object | no | A new script (or new steps for one) to run, saved with the automation |
| `scriptText.name` | string | yes |  |
| `scriptText.text` | string | yes | One step per line, as the script workspace shows them |
| `parameter` | string | no | Formula on the record for Get ( ScriptParameter ) |
| `account` | string | no | Account the script runs as (default: this one) |
| `network` | boolean | no | Let Insert from URL reach the network (only if the server allows scripts the network too) |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | Whether it runs once saved (default true) |
| `test` | object of string or number | no | The change that sets it off, field name to new value (e.g. {"Status": "Paid"}), made on a throwaway copy |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "try_automation",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "name": "Paid date",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "on": "update",
    "fields": [
      "Status"
    ],
    "condition": "Status = \"Paid\"",
    "scriptText": {
      "name": "Stamp paid",
      "text": "Set Field [ Invoices::Customer ; Upper ( Invoices::Customer ) ]"
    },
    "test": {
      "Status": "Paid"
    }
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "trigger": "When a record in Invoices is changed, and the change is to Status, if Status = \"Paid\": run \"Stamp paid\" on that record (from layout Invoices) as Admin",
  "dryRun": {
    "recordId": 1,
    "setOff": [
      "Status: \"Open\" → \"Paid\" on record 1"
    ],
    "conditionTrue": true,
    "outcome": "ok",
    "steps": 1,
    "changes": [
      "Sets Invoices::Customer to \"ACME CORP\" on record 1"
    ],
    "outbound": []
  }
}
```

<a id="save-automation"></a>

### `save_automation`

Automations, step two: save (and turn on) an automation tried with try_automation, writing its script if scriptText is given. It runs on the server for every matching change, whoever makes it, offline unless network is allowed; its own changes set off no automations. Saving over one with the same name needs replace: true; enabled: false turns one off.

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** [Full Access] or the server administrator. The automation runs as the account named, by default the one saving it.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `name` | string | yes | The automation's name |
| `description` | string | no | What it does, in a sentence |
| `layout` | string | yes | Its table's records are watched; the script runs from this layout on the record |
| `on` | "create" \\| "update" \\| "createOrUpdate" \\| "delete" | yes | What sets it off; delete: the script gets the deleted record as JSON in Get ( ScriptParameter ), with no fields, condition or parameter |
| `fields` | array of string | no | update: only when one of these fields changed ("when Status changes") |
| `condition` | string | no | FileMaker formula on the record after the change; runs only when true (Status = "Paid") |
| `script` | string | no | An existing script to run; or give scriptText |
| `scriptText` | object | no | A new script (or new steps for one) to run, saved with the automation |
| `scriptText.name` | string | yes |  |
| `scriptText.text` | string | yes | One step per line, as the script workspace shows them |
| `parameter` | string | no | Formula on the record for Get ( ScriptParameter ) |
| `account` | string | no | Account the script runs as (default: this one) |
| `network` | boolean | no | Let Insert from URL reach the network (only if the server allows scripts the network too) |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | Whether it runs now (default true) |
| `replace` | boolean | no | true to save over an automation with the same name |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "save_automation",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "name": "Paid date",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "on": "update",
    "fields": [
      "Status"
    ],
    "condition": "Status = \"Paid\"",
    "script": "Mark Paid"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "saved": true,
  "automation": {
    "name": "Paid date",
    "enabled": true,
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "on": "update",
    "fields": [
      "Status"
    ],
    "condition": "Status = \"Paid\"",
    "script": "Mark Paid",
    "account": "Admin",
    "id": "841a547c2332",
    "created": "2026-10-13T09:40:13.859Z",
    "updated": "2026-10-13T09:40:13.859Z",
    "createdBy": "Admin"
  },
  "trigger": "When a record in Invoices is changed, and the change is to Status, if Status = \"Paid\": run \"Mark Paid\" on that record (from layout Invoices) as Admin"
}
```

<a id="delete-automation"></a>

### `delete_automation`

Delete an automation (by name or id). Its script stays.

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** [Full Access] or the server administrator.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `automation` | string | yes | The automation's name or id |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "delete_automation",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "automation": "Paid date"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "deleted": "Paid date"
}
```

<a id="list-connections"></a>

### `list_connections`

The outside services this server can connect to, by name (S3-compatible storage: Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, MinIO, Wasabi; REST web APIs; and email accounts for Send Mail): each one's settings, whether it is a draft (waiting for a person), on or off, which files may use it, and which of its secrets are set (never their values). Also the types, with the settings each takes and the well-known services (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive) with the settings that point a REST connection at them. Scripts use a connection with Insert from URL and "connection://name/folder/file"; the keys stay on the server.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] or the server administrator; not a limited token. Never returns a secret, only whether each is set.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "list_connections",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "types": [
    {
      "id": "s3",
      "label": "S3-compatible storage",
      "description": "Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, MinIO, Wasabi or anything that speaks the S3 protocol",
      "settings": [
        {
          "name": "bucket",
          "label": "Bucket",
          "required": true
        }
      ],
      "secrets": [
        {
          "name": "accessKey",
          "label": "Access key ID",
          "required": true
        },
        {
          "name": "secretKey",
          "label": "Secret access key",
          "required": true
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "connections": [
    {
      "name": "invoices-bucket",
      "type": "s3",
      "status": "active",
      "settings": {
        "bucket": "acme-invoices",
        "region": "us-east-1",
        "prefix": "tabularius"
      },
      "files": [
        "Invoices"
      ],
      "draftedByAi": true,
      "secrets": [
        {
          "name": "accessKey",
          "set": true
        },
        {
          "name": "secretKey",
          "set": true
        },
        {
          "name": "sessionToken",
          "set": false
        }
      ],
      "ready": true
    }
  ]
}
```

status is draft (waiting for a person to add the keys and approve it in the admin console), active or disabled. Scripts use an active connection with Insert from URL and an address like connection://invoices-bucket/2026/scan.pdf.

<a id="draft-connection"></a>

### `draft_connection`

Set up a connection to an outside service from what the person asked ("set up an S3 connection to our invoices bucket"): this makes a DRAFT with the settings they gave (type, bucket, region, endpoint for R2/B2/MinIO, a folder in the bucket) and nothing else. It does nothing yet: a person opens the admin console's Connections page, checks the settings, types the access key and secret key into the secret boxes, tests it and approves it. You never see, ask for, accept or invent keys or passwords: if the person offers one in chat, tell them to put it in the console and not here (a setting that looks like a key is refused). Ask them for any setting you need (the bucket name; the endpoint when it isn't Amazon S3) rather than guessing. The draft is limited to this file, and its name is what scripts call it by. You can't change, approve, turn on or remove a connection.

**Permissions:** [Full Access] or the server administrator; not a limited token, and never for a capture-only file. Makes a draft only: it can't set a key, approve, turn on, change or remove a connection, and at most 10 AI drafts wait at once.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `name` | string | yes | What scripts call it: letters, digits, dashes, underscores, starting with a letter, e.g. "invoices-bucket" |
| `type` | "s3" \\| "rest" \\| "smtp" | yes | The kind of service (see list_connections) |
| `config` | object of string | yes | The type's settings (see list_connections), e.g. {"bucket": "acme-invoices", "region": "us-east-1", "prefix": "tabularius"}. Never a key or password. |
| `note` | string | no | What it is for, shown to the person who approves it |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "draft_connection",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "name": "invoices-bucket",
    "type": "s3",
    "config": {
      "bucket": "acme-invoices",
      "region": "us-east-1",
      "prefix": "tabularius"
    },
    "note": "Scanned invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "drafted": true,
  "name": "invoices-bucket",
  "type": "s3",
  "status": "draft",
  "settings": {
    "bucket": "acme-invoices",
    "region": "us-east-1",
    "prefix": "tabularius"
  },
  "forFile": "Invoices",
  "next": "Nothing is connected yet. A person has to open the admin console > Connections, check these settings, type the access key and secret key into the secret boxes (they never go through chat or this tool), press Test, and approve it."
}
```

The AI never sees, asks for or invents a key: a setting that looks like one (an AWS access key, a private key, a token) is refused, and keys can only be set by a person in the console. The draft is limited to the file it was made from until a person changes that.

<a id="conversion-report"></a>

### `conversion_report`

What in a converted FileMaker file won't work yet in Tabularius: script steps the engine can't run, FileMaker functions not available yet, plug-in functions, formulas that don't parse, other files the solution uses that aren't hosted, and accounts without a password. Also steps that never run (Send Mail), steps that need the network, and references already broken in FileMaker. Each item has a count and the first places it appears. Pass item (a script, field, layout, table, custom function or value list) for why that one doesn't work as it did in FileMaker: every place in it, the scripts it performs that have problems, and files it needs that aren't hosted.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access], or a set that can modify scripts and read everything (designAccess); not available to scoped API tokens.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `item` | string | no | Name of one script, field (Table::Field), layout, table, custom function or value list |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "conversion_report",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "summary": "# Conversion report: Invoices\n\nNothing found that won't work.\n\n## Good to know\n- **Never run**: Send Mail (1). Tabularius doesn't send email.\n- **Privilege sets imported**: [Full Access] (full access; fmapp, fmwebdirect, fmrest).\n- **Record access is imported at the whole-file level.** FileMaker's per-table, per-layout, per-value-list and per-script \"Custom privileges\" aren't decoded yet, so a set that used them is approximated by its overall access — review those sets in Manage Security.",
  "functions": {
    "notYet": [],
    "undecoded": [],
    "plugIns": []
  },
  "steps": {
    "notYet": [],
    "blocked": [
      {
        "name": "Send Mail",
        "count": 1,
        "where": [
          "Script \"Email Invoice\", line 2"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "network": [],
    "screenOnly": [],
    "clientOnly": []
  },
  "unparsed": [],
  "broken": [],
  "commentedOut": [],
  "dataSources": [],
  "accounts": {
    "withoutPassword": [],
    "blankPassword": []
  },
  "externalContainers": {
    "files": 0,
    "missing": 0,
    "examples": []
  },
  "privileges": {
    "assignments": [
      {
        "account": "Admin",
        "privilegeSet": "[Full Access]"
      }
    ],
    "withoutSet": [],
    "sets": [
      {
        "name": "[Full Access]",
        "records": "full access",
        "extended": [
          "fmapp",
          "fmwebdirect",
          "fmrest"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "coarsened": true
  }
}
```

With item the result is Markdown about that one item, e.g. "# script Email Invoice\nWhat won't work as it did in FileMaker:\n- Send Mail (Never runs here: Tabularius doesn't send email): line 2".

<a id="conversion-guide"></a>

### `conversion_guide`

The plain-English guide to a converted file, written when it was converted (or converted again): what won't work until changed (plug-ins, steps and functions not available yet, tables in SQL databases, other files not hosted), what works differently (Send Mail sends nothing, Insert from URL stays offline, web viewers that load internet pages show a placeholder, screen-only steps skipped on the server, privilege sets imported at the whole-file level), the built-in replacement for each, and what to do before people use it. Secrets in scripts are hidden. Markdown.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access], or a set that can modify scripts and read everything (designAccess); not available to scoped API tokens.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "conversion_guide",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```text
# Invoices: what to know after converting

## Won't work until changed
- **MBS (MonkeyBread) plug-in** (1): 1 call in 1 script. No plug-ins run here, so each call gives an error.
  Instead: Send Mail [ Send via SMTP Server ; … ] (Tabularius sends no mail unless the server is set up to).
  Where: Script "Email Invoice", line 1

## Works differently
- **Send Mail** (1): Sends nothing: the step ends with error 3 and the script carries on. A server set up for test mode keeps each message in the admin console's outbox instead.
  Instead: Keep the step as it is (Send via SMTP Server) for when the server is set up to send mail.
  Where: Script "Email Invoice", line 2

## Before people use it
- Move off plug-ins one script at a time: ask the assistant ("replace the MBS (MonkeyBread) plug-in") or an MCP client (migration_plan); each rewritten script is tried offline on a copy first.
```

Markdown. Only what the design shows: items found by reading the records (such as the names of container files) are left out.

<a id="optimization-report"></a>

### `optimization_report`

Ways to make a converted file smaller and faster, worst first, each with what it would save and what to do: container files kept inside the file (size by field: S3 or managed external storage instead, and only a link kept), sorts and matches on unstored calculations or fields without an index in big tables, fields, scripts, table occurrences and value lists nothing uses, wide tables, repeating fields, long value lists. It changes nothing; a finding that has an action says so, and a person approves it first. Markdown, or JSON with json: true.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access], or a set that can modify scripts and read everything (designAccess); not available to scoped API tokens.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `json` | boolean | no | The findings as JSON, with their actions and the requests that carry them out |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "optimization_report",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```text
# Invoices: ways to make it smaller and faster

The converted file is 26.0 MB. 24.8 MB of that is 405 container files stored inside it, 151 pictures among them (6.7 MB).

## High impact
- **Container files inside the file: Assets::Photo** (saves up to 21.1 MB; 8): 8 files totalling 21.1 MB (81% of the converted file) are stored in the database itself, 5 pictures (6.1 MB) of them; the largest is 12.9 MB. Every backup, copy and replica carries them.
  Instead: Move them to S3-compatible storage and keep only a link in the record (the database shrinks by this much and pictures are served from storage), or to managed external storage next to the file.
  Where: Assets::Photo

## Housekeeping
- **Scripts nothing runs** (2): 2 scripts are performed by no script, button, trigger or custom menu. People may still run them from the Scripts menu, a schedule or the Data API.
  Instead: Remove the ones nobody runs, or keep them in a folder named for what they are (utilities, old).
  Where: Old import; Test
```

Changes nothing. Markdown, or the findings as JSON with json: true: each has an impact (high, medium, low), the bytes it would save, and any action with the admin API request that carries it out (an index is added with POST /tabularius/admin/v1/indexes); moving container files to S3 is described and marked unavailable until an S3 connection is set up.

<a id="optimization-fix"></a>

### `optimization_fix`

Makes one of the fixes optimization_report offers for a hosted file: hide or remove the scripts, value lists or table occurrences nothing uses, or store an unstored calculation a sort depends on. Without confirm: true it only lists exactly what it would do and changes nothing, so show that to a person and make the change only when they approve. Each fix is one change, and undo: true puts the latest one back (or the one with that id). Removing a script or value list is not for you to decide: a person may still use it from outside the file.

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** [Full Access], or a set that can modify scripts and read everything (designAccess); not available to scoped API tokens.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `fix` | "hide-scripts" \\| "remove-scripts" \\| "remove-value-lists" \\| "remove-table-occurrences" \\| "store-calculation" | no | Which fix, as optimization_report names it in a finding's actions |
| `items` | array of string | no | Which ones, by name (a calculation as Table::Field); all that the report lists when left out, except for store-calculation |
| `confirm` | boolean | no | true makes the change; left out, the call only says what it would do |
| `undo` | boolean or number | no | true puts back the latest fix, or the number of an earlier one (the report lists them) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "optimization_fix",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "fix": "remove-value-lists"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "fix": "remove-value-lists",
  "label": "Remove 1 value list",
  "will": [
    "Remove the value list \"Colours\"."
  ],
  "count": 1,
  "undoable": true,
  "note": "Nothing was changed. Send confirm: true once a person has approved this."
}
```

Makes one of the fixes optimization_report offers: hide-scripts, remove-scripts, remove-value-lists, remove-table-occurrences, or store-calculation (items: ["Table::Field"]). Without confirm: true it only lists what it would do. Each fix is one change; undo: true (or the number of an earlier fix) puts it back. Removing is a decision for a person: scripts and value lists may be used from outside the file.

<a id="optimization-move-containers"></a>

### `optimization_move_containers`

Moves the container files a converted file keeps inside its database (the optimization report names the fields) out to managed external storage: one file each, in the field's folder beside the hosted file, and the file is then rewritten so it shrinks. If the field doesn't store its files outside the file yet, it is set to (a design change). All or nothing, and undone with undo. Without confirm: true it only describes what would happen. Needs [Full Access].

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** [Full Access] only (it changes the file and writes files beside it); not available to scoped API tokens. The assistant does not get this tool.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `table` | string | no | Table of the container field (with field) |
| `field` | string | no | The container field whose files are moved |
| `expect` | integer | no | How many files the report said the field keeps inside the file; a different count now refuses the move (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |
| `confirm` | boolean | no | true makes the move; otherwise it is only described (default false) |
| `undo` | integer | no | The number of an earlier move (listed with the report) to put back (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "optimization_move_containers",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "table": "Assets",
    "field": "Photo",
    "expect": 8
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "plan": {
    "table": "Assets",
    "field": "Photo",
    "files": 8,
    "bytes": 22100000,
    "folder": "RC_Data_FMS/Invoices/Assets/Photo/",
    "setsStorage": true,
    "preview": [
      "Move 8 files (21 MB) of Assets::Photo out of the database into the folder RC_Data_FMS/Invoices/Assets/Photo/ beside the hosted file.",
      "…"
    ]
  },
  "message": "Nothing was changed. Call again with confirm: true to make this move."
}
```

Without confirm: true it only describes the move. With it, the files move out (all or nothing), the field is set to store its files outside the file if it wasn't, and the file is rewritten so it shrinks; the result has the move (move.id). Pass undo with that number (and confirm: true) to put the files back; call with no table and field to list the moves that can be undone. Files the folder has lost since are left as they are and counted in missing.

<a id="migration-plan"></a>

### `migration_plan`

Moving a converted file off its plug-ins (360Works Email, MBS, BaseElements, Troi, DataGuard, ...): every plug-in call, grouped by plug-in, with how often and where, whether it works here already, and the native FileMaker replacement (Send Mail via SMTP for mail plug-ins, Insert from URL for HTTP, JSON and Crypt functions, data file steps). Also the scripts to rewrite, most calls first, and the formulas that call plug-ins. Rewrite one script at a time: try_design_change dry-runs a rewritten script offline on a copy before it is applied.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access], or a set that can modify scripts and read everything (designAccess); not available to scoped API tokens.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name (the .fmp12 file name without extension) |
| `plugIn` | string | no | Only this plug-in ("360Works Email", "MBS", "BaseElements") |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "migration_plan",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "summary": "Plug-in calls: MBS (MonkeyBread) (1), in 1 script and 0 formulas. Rewrite one script at a time: each rewritten script is dry-run offline on a copy of the file before anyone applies it.",
  "plugIns": [
    {
      "plugIn": "MBS (MonkeyBread)",
      "calls": [
        {
          "call": "MBS ( \"SMTP.Send\" )",
          "count": 1,
          "worksHere": false,
          "native": "Send Mail [ Send via SMTP Server ; … ] (Tabularius sends no mail unless the server is set up to).",
          "where": [
            "Script \"Email Invoice\", line 1"
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "scripts": [
    {
      "script": "Email Invoice",
      "calls": 1,
      "plugIns": [
        "MBS (MonkeyBread)"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "formulas": []
}
```

<a id="compare-solutions"></a>

### `compare_solutions`

Compare two hosted databases, usually two versions of one solution (staged against live, a backup against today's file): tables, fields (type, formula, options), table occurrences, relationships, layouts (fields and buttons on them), scripts (with a line diff), value lists, custom functions, accounts, privilege sets and record counts that were added, removed, renamed or changed. Versions of one file are matched by FileMaker's ids, so renames show as renames.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** Design access (designAccess) in both files: [Full Access], or a set that can modify scripts and read everything; not available to scoped API tokens. Accounts and privilege sets are compared only with [Full Access] (or as the administrator) in both.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | string | yes | The older or reference database |
| `to` | string | yes | The newer database |
| `scriptDiffLines` | integer | no | Changed lines to show per script (default 40, min 0, max 500) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "compare_solutions",
  "arguments": {
    "from": "Invoices",
    "to": "Invoices Staging"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "from": "Invoices",
  "to": "Invoices Staging",
  "matchedBy": "id",
  "summary": "fields: 1 added; layouts: 1 changed.",
  "fields": {
    "added": [
      "Invoices::Notes"
    ]
  },
  "layouts": {
    "changed": [
      {
        "name": "Invoices",
        "details": [
          "fields added: Invoices::Notes"
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<a id="get-design"></a>

### `get_design`

Design of a database for design work, with ids: tables with every field option, table occurrences, relationships with match fields, File Options (startup layout and scripts), value lists, custom functions, custom menus, layouts, scripts as text. Pick sections; for a large solution, a call without sections lists them with their sizes. Scripts come as text; name scripts to get their steps with decoded options too.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `sections` | array of "tables" \\| "tableOccurrences" \\| "relationships" \\| "dataSources" \\| "containerDirectories" \\| "containerData" \\| "fileOptions" \\| "pageSetup" \\| "valueLists" \\| "customFunctions" \\| "deleted" \\| "customMenus" \\| "customMenuSets" \\| "defaultMenuSetId" \\| "menuCommands" \\| "layouts" \\| "layoutOrder" \\| "scripts" \\| "scriptOrder" \\| "themes" \\| "privilegeSets" \\| "scriptSteps" | no | Default: all, when that is small enough |
| `scripts` | array of string | no | Only these scripts, with their steps' decoded options (at most 50 items) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "get_design",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "sections": [
      "layouts",
      "scripts"
    ]
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "layouts": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "name": "Customers",
      "tableOccurrenceId": 129,
      "occurrence": "Customers"
    },
    {
      "id": 2,
      "name": "Invoices",
      "tableOccurrenceId": 130,
      "occurrence": "Invoices"
    }
  ],
  "scripts": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "name": "Mark paid",
      "text": "Set Field [ Invoices::Status ; \"Paid\" ]\nCommit Records/Requests [ With dialog: Off ]"
    }
  ]
}
```

Without sections the whole design comes back when it is 25,000 characters or less; above that the result is {database, note, sections: {section: size in characters}} so the client can ask for sections. Scripts named in `scripts` also carry their steps with decoded options. Secrets in script text and custom function formulas are redacted.
