<a id="lint-script"></a>

### `lint_script`

Check scripts for loops that never end and guards that catch nothing, which FileMaker never warns about: a loop with no way out (Go to Record [ Next ] without “Exit after last”), Exit Loop If [ $count = $i ] when $i starts at 1 and the count can be 0, a loop that omits records and only ends on “Exit after last” in another branch, and IsValid used to ask whether there is a related record. Each issue gives the step, its line, what goes wrong in plain English, a fix, and detail: why (for a count, where it comes from and when it is 0, such as a parameter the script never got). Leave out script to check every script. Nothing runs.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `script` | string or integer | no | The script's name or id; leave out to check every script |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "lint_script",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "scripts": [
    {
      "script": "Loop invoices",
      "issues": [
        {
          "rule": "loop-no-exit",
          "severity": "error",
          "step": 3,
          "line": 4,
          "message": "Go to Record/Request/Page [ Next ] stays on the last record when there is no other one, and nothing else ends this loop, so it never stops.",
          "fix": "Turn on “Exit after last”: Go to Record/Request/Page [ Next ; Exit after last: On ]",
          "detail": "FileMaker gives error 101 on the last record and stays there; without “Exit after last” the loop goes on with that record forever."
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Without script, only scripts with issues are listed; with script, that script is listed even when it has none.

<a id="lint-layout"></a>

### `lint_layout`

Check a layout for what will look or behave wrong in Browse mode: fields showing <Field Missing> or nothing (occurrence not related to the layout's), objects outside the layout, clickable objects on top of each other, buttons with no action, enterable fields left out of the tab order, and fields some privilege sets see as <No Access>; rule "slow" is what makes the layout slow to draw (unstored related totals, summaries on every row, portal filters), with cost = estimated record reads per draw from the file's record counts. Each issue names the object ids; fix them with change_design updateLayout or edit_layout_objects.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `layout` | string or integer | yes | The layout's name or id |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "lint_layout",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "layout": "Invoices",
  "issues": [
    {
      "rule": "overlap",
      "severity": "warning",
      "objectIds": [
        10,
        7
      ],
      "message": "Invoices::Status covers Invoices::CustomerId: people may click the wrong one. Move one of them.",
      "fixable": true
    },
    {
      "rule": "no-action",
      "severity": "warning",
      "objectIds": [
        11
      ],
      "message": "\"Pay\" does nothing when clicked: give it a script or a step in Button Setup."
    }
  ]
}
```

Rule "slow" is what makes the layout slow to draw (unstored related totals, summaries on every row, portal filters); its issues carry cost, the estimated record reads per draw from the file's record counts. speed_up_layout redesigns those where there is a mechanical way.

<a id="check-solution"></a>

### `check_solution`

Look through the whole solution for what is wrong, without running anything: calculations that do not parse or name a field, function, script, layout or value list that is not there; layout objects and relationships that point at a deleted field; value lists with no source; script steps and plug-in functions this build does not run (error 3, or "?"); privilege sets that name things that are gone or grant nothing; accounts with no privilege set; and, as information only, scripts, value lists and custom functions nothing uses. Each finding has a kind, severity (error, warning, info), where it is, what is wrong and a one-line fix. With account, also what that account cannot reach (a button for a script it may not run, the layout the file opens on). The same check as `tabularius check-solution`. For one script or calculation use check_script, check_calculation and lint_script.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `account` | string | no | Also check what this account can reach |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "check_solution",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "counts": {
    "error": 1,
    "warning": 0,
    "info": 1
  },
  "findings": [
    {
      "kind": "missing-script",
      "severity": "error",
      "where": "Script \"New invoice\", line 3",
      "message": "There is no script named \"helper\" (did you mean \"Helper\"?).",
      "hint": "Point the step at a script that exists, or add the script."
    },
    {
      "kind": "unused-value-list",
      "severity": "info",
      "where": "Value list \"Cities\"",
      "message": "No field or layout object uses it.",
      "hint": "Delete it if it is not needed."
    }
  ]
}
```

Nothing runs and nothing changes. Errors come first. With account, findings also say what that account cannot reach. The same check as `tabularius check-solution` (see docs/check-solution.md).

<a id="fix-layout"></a>

### `fix_layout`

Mend lint_layout's mechanical findings on a layout in one change: nearly lined-up edges lined up, clickable objects on top of each other moved apart, objects running past the layout's edge moved inside, and the tab order given the fields it skips (in reading order), fields with no label labelled with their name, buttons with no text given a tooltip naming their script, fields and buttons too small to tap on a phone layout grown, and fields a portal sorts on with indexing off given automatic indexing, and summary fields on every row of a list moved into a trailing grand summary. Only findings with fixable: true; the rest need a person. With preview: true nothing is saved.

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `layout` | string or integer | yes | The layout's name or id |
| `only` | array of object | no | Fix just these findings (from lint_layout); default all fixable ones |
| `only[].rule` | string | yes |  |
| `only[].objectIds` | array of integer | yes |  |
| `preview` | boolean | no | Say what would be fixed, without saving (default false) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "fix_layout",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "layout": "Invoices",
  "fixed": [
    "Invoices::Status covers Invoices::CustomerId: people may click the wrong one. Move one of them.",
    "\"Wide\" runs past the layout's right edge, so part of it is cut off."
  ],
  "saved": true,
  "remaining": []
}
```

Saved changes are recorded in the design history under the account "AI". remaining is what lint_layout still finds on the result. Besides the other fixes, a summary field on every row of a list moves into a trailing grand summary.

<a id="speed-up-layout"></a>

### `speed_up_layout`

Make a slow layout faster (FileMaker has no such tool): for each of lint_layout's "slow" findings, a redesign that removes the work where there is a mechanical one: a summary field on every row moved into a trailing grand summary, an unstored calculation or related summary on every row shown from a new stored calculation (which can fall behind related records; the caveat says so). Each move has the layout's estimated record reads per draw before and after. Portal filters and formulas come back in left: redesign those yourself with change_design (a relationship that matches the records instead of a filter). With apply: [move indexes] those moves are saved as one change and undo is returned; otherwise nothing is saved.

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `layout` | string or integer | yes | The layout's name or id |
| `apply` | array of integer | no | Indexes into moves to save |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "speed_up_layout",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Customers"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "layout": "Customers",
  "before": 2000,
  "moves": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "kind": "unstored calculation",
      "objectIds": [
        901
      ],
      "title": "Show Customers::Billed from a new stored calculation, Customers::Billed stored",
      "caveat": "Billed stored is worked out when its own record changes, not when the related records change, so it can fall behind them; Stale stored values in the admin console brings it up to date.",
      "after": 1000
    }
  ],
  "left": [
    {
      "kind": "portal filter",
      "objectIds": [
        902
      ],
      "message": "The portal's filter is worked out for every related Invoices record (about 100), on every row (about 1,000 record reads each time the layout draws). Match the records in the relationship instead (another match field, or a global key), so the index does the filtering.",
      "cost": 1000
    }
  ],
  "saved": false
}
```

before and each move's after are the layout's estimated record reads per draw. Without apply nothing is saved. With apply: [indexes into moves] each chosen move is worked out again on the layout as the earlier ones left it and saved (recorded in the design history under the account "AI"), and the result also has saved, applied (the indexes saved), skipped (moves an earlier one made unnecessary), error (a move that could not be saved, which stops the rest; those already saved stay), after (the reads per draw now) and undo (the changes that take the saved moves back, last first, left out when one of them can't be undone). An index outside moves is an error and nothing is saved.

<a id="review-graph"></a>

### `review_graph`

Look over the relationship graph: a plain-English account of its groups (and whether it follows anchor-buoy), and the problems worth a look: occurrences nothing uses, relationships that repeat another in the same group, match fields that can't be indexed (globals, unstored calculations, summaries, containers) or have indexing off, and missing tables or fields. Each issue names occurrence ids (and a relationship id). Use it to explain the graph to a person or to propose fixes.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "review_graph",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "summary": [
    "The graph has 2 table occurrences of 2 tables, joined by 1 relationship into 1 group.",
    "Customers (1 layout) reaches Invoices; Invoices also has layouts.",
    "Nothing looks wrong."
  ],
  "groups": [
    {
      "anchor": 129,
      "occurrences": [
        129,
        130
      ],
      "anchorBuoy": false
    }
  ],
  "issues": [],
  "boxesToTidy": 2
}
```

<a id="arrange-graph"></a>

### `arrange_graph`

Tidy the relationship graph's boxes in one change: each group laid out from its anchor (the occurrence layouts are based on) in columns to the right, groups stacked top to bottom, lone occurrences in a grid at the end. Only positions change. With preview: true nothing is saved.

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `preview` | boolean | no | Say how many boxes would move, without saving (default false) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "arrange_graph",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "moved": 2,
  "saved": true
}
```

Saved changes are recorded in the design history under the account "AI".

<a id="restyle-layout"></a>

### `restyle_layout`

Restyle a layout: make it look like another layout (its theme, and each kind of object's most common style and formatting, part by part), switch it to a theme, and/or apply the theme consistently (drop local formatting so every object shows its theme style). Only looks change: nothing moves. With preview: true (the default) nothing is saved; it says what would change and what Check finds on the result. Undo is returned when saved.

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `layout` | string or integer | yes | The layout to restyle, by name or id |
| `like` | string or integer | no | The layout to take the look from |
| `theme` | string or integer | no | A theme to switch to, by name or id |
| `consistent` | boolean | no | Drop local formatting so objects show their theme styles |
| `preview` | boolean | no | true (the default) shows what would change and saves nothing (default true) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "restyle_layout",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "theme": "House"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "layout": "Invoices",
  "notes": [
    "Theme: none → House."
  ],
  "check": [],
  "saved": false
}
```

preview defaults to true. With preview: false the result also has undo: updateLayout changes that put the layouts back as they were.

<a id="restyle-file"></a>

### `restyle_file`

Restyle every layout in a file at once (FileMaker restyles one layout at a time): onto an existing theme, or onto a new theme made from a few design tokens (accent, accentText, text, muted, background, panel, line: #rrggbb colours; font; size and radius in points; tabularius's own look for any left out). consistent also drops local formatting. layouts limits it to those ids. Phone layouts that follow their desktop layout stay in step. With preview: true (the default) nothing is saved; it says what would change on each layout. Undo is returned when saved.

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `theme` | string or integer | no | An existing theme, by name or id |
| `tokens` | object | no | A new theme from these tokens (instead of theme) |
| `tokens.accent` | string | no |  |
| `tokens.accentText` | string | no |  |
| `tokens.text` | string | no |  |
| `tokens.muted` | string | no |  |
| `tokens.background` | string | no |  |
| `tokens.panel` | string | no |  |
| `tokens.line` | string | no |  |
| `tokens.font` | string | no |  |
| `tokens.size` | number | no |  |
| `tokens.radius` | number | no |  |
| `name` | string | no | The new theme's name (default House) |
| `consistent` | boolean | no | true also drops local formatting so every object takes the theme's style |
| `layouts` | array of integer | no | Only these layout ids (default every layout) |
| `preview` | boolean | no | true (the default) shows what would change on each layout and saves nothing (default true) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "restyle_file",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "tokens": {
      "accent": "#224488"
    },
    "name": "Blue"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "theme": "Blue",
  "layouts": [
    {
      "name": "Customers",
      "notes": [
        "Theme: none → Blue."
      ],
      "check": {
        "before": 0,
        "after": 0
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "Invoices",
      "notes": [
        "Theme: none → Blue."
      ],
      "check": {
        "before": 0,
        "after": 0
      }
    }
  ],
  "unchanged": [],
  "saved": false
}
```

preview defaults to true. With preview: false the result also has undo.

<a id="modernize-interfaces"></a>

### `modernize_interfaces`

Make new layouts for a file's tables from ready-made templates, with no AI: for each table a modern list, a modern detail (one record with Previous and Next), a modern list and detail side by side (HTML, CSS and JavaScript pages that search, sort, edit, add and delete records as the signed-in account and show related records), and a classic FileMaker list and form drafted the way the file's own layouts look. Columns and controls come from the fields' types and names; join tables of only keys get none. The file's own layouts are never changed, and a layout that is already there is left alone. tables and styles (modern-list, modern-detail, modern-split, classic-list, classic-form; and, only when asked for, modern-board: cards in columns by a status field, and modern-calendar: records on a month by a date field) narrow it; fromLayouts: true also makes a modern list and detail for each of the file's own layouts, with the fields that layout shows in its order; the new layouts go in a "Modernized interfaces" folder unless folder is false. With preview: true (the default) nothing is saved; it returns the layouts, the tables skipped and why, and the changes. Undo is returned when saved.

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `tables` | array of string | no | Only these tables (default every table) (at most 500 items) |
| `styles` | array of "modern-list" \\| "modern-detail" \\| "modern-split" \\| "classic-list" \\| "classic-form" \\| "modern-board" \\| "modern-calendar" | no | Only these kinds of layout (default all of them) |
| `folder` | boolean | no | false puts the new layouts at the top level instead of in a "Modernized interfaces" folder |
| `fromLayouts` | boolean | no | true builds a modern copy of each existing layout, following the fields that layout shows, instead of a generic one per table |
| `preview` | boolean | no | true (the default) lists the layouts and saves nothing (default true) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "modernize_interfaces",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "tables": [
      "Invoices"
    ],
    "styles": [
      "modern-list",
      "classic-form"
    ]
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "layouts": [
    {
      "name": "Invoices - Modern list",
      "table": "Invoices",
      "style": "modern-list",
      "notes": [
        "Columns: Number, Status, Due, Amount."
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "Invoices - Classic form",
      "table": "Invoices",
      "style": "classic-form",
      "notes": [
        "Theme House, the one 1 layout in the file uses."
      ]
    }
  ],
  "skipped": [
    {
      "table": "InvoiceTags",
      "why": "only keys and stamps, which looks like a join table"
    }
  ],
  "saved": false
}
```

preview defaults to true. With preview: false the layouts are made in a "Modernized interfaces" folder and the result also has undo. Nothing the file already has is changed.

<a id="draft-layout"></a>

### `draft_layout`

Draft a new layout that looks like the file's own: the theme most of its layouts use (or like: another layout's), fields, labels, title and parts styled as they most often are there, and the components the file keeps in its headers and footers placed where they usually sit. totals: number fields to total in a grand summary (summary fields are added) or existing summary fields (list view). A layout keeps no find, so find ({field: criterion}, omit) and sort add a "Show <layout>" script that goes to it and finds those records. portals (form view): related records as a portal ({occurrence, fields, rows, totals: columns to total under it, as Sum calculations}). A report: groups (sub-summaries; a date by month, quarter or year), summaryOnly, and chart (one point per group); the script sorts by the groups. arrangement: when copying a picture of a layout (a screenshot, a sketch), where it shows each thing, in points from its part's top left, with the file's real fields; it replaces fields, totals and portals. Check's mechanical fixes are applied to the draft. With preview: true (the default) nothing is saved; it returns the changes, how the draft matches the file and what Check finds on it. Undo is returned when saved.

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `name` | string | yes | The new layout's name (at least 1 characters) |
| `occurrence` | string or integer | yes | The table occurrence the layout shows, by name or id |
| `view` | "list" \\| "form" | no | list (rows) or form (one record) (default "list") |
| `fields` | array of string | no | Fields to show, in order |
| `totals` | array of string | no | Number fields to total in a grand summary, or existing summary fields |
| `like` | string or integer | no | The layout to take the look from |
| `find` | object of string | no | Field name to find criterion |
| `omit` | boolean | no | true makes the find leave out the matches instead of finding them |
| `sort` | array of string | no | Fields to sort by |
| `portals` | array of object | no | Form only: portals of related records |
| `portals[].occurrence` | string or integer | yes |  |
| `portals[].fields` | array of string | no |  |
| `portals[].rows` | integer | no | (min 1, max 50) |
| `portals[].totals` | array of string | no |  |
| `arrangement` | object | no | From a picture: the layout as it shows it |
| `arrangement.width` | number | yes |  |
| `arrangement.parts` | array of object | yes |  |
| `arrangement.parts[].kind` | "header" \\| "body" \\| "trailing-grand-summary" \\| "footer" | yes |  |
| `arrangement.parts[].height` | number | yes |  |
| `arrangement.objects` | array of object | yes | (at most 300 items) |
| `arrangement.objects[].kind` | "field" \\| "label" \\| "title" \\| "button" \\| "portal" \\| "rectangle" \\| "line" | yes |  |
| `arrangement.objects[].part` | integer | yes | (min 0, max 9007199254740991) |
| `arrangement.objects[].left` | number | yes |  |
| `arrangement.objects[].top` | number | yes |  |
| `arrangement.objects[].width` | number | yes |  |
| `arrangement.objects[].height` | number | yes |  |
| `arrangement.objects[].field` | string | no | "Field", or "Occurrence::Field" of a related occurrence |
| `arrangement.objects[].text` | string | no |  |
| `arrangement.objects[].portal` | object | no |  |
| `arrangement.objects[].portal.occurrence` | string | yes |  |
| `arrangement.objects[].portal.fields` | array of string | yes | (at most 20 items) |
| `arrangement.objects[].portal.rows` | integer | no | (min 1, max 50) |
| `groups` | array of string or object | no | List only, a report: fields to group by in sub-summaries, outermost first; a date by month, quarter or year |
| `summaryOnly` | boolean | no | Only the groups' totals, no row per record |
| `chart` | object | no | A chart of the found set at the top, one point per group; value is a number field to total or a summary field |
| `chart.type` | "column" \\| "bar" \\| "line" \\| "area" \\| "pie" | no | (default "column") |
| `chart.value` | string | yes |  |
| `chart.by` | string | no |  |
| `chart.title` | string | no |  |
| `preview` | boolean | no | true (the default) returns the draft and saves nothing (default true) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "draft_layout",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "name": "Invoice list draft",
    "occurrence": "Invoices",
    "fields": [
      "Number",
      "Total"
    ],
    "preview": false
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "layout": "Invoice list draft",
  "notes": [
    "Theme House, the one 1 layout in the file uses.",
    "Fields, labels, title and parts styled as they most often are on the file's 1 layout with that theme."
  ],
  "check": [],
  "saved": true,
  "undo": [
    {
      "op": "deleteLayout",
      "layout": 3
    }
  ]
}
```

preview defaults to true; a preview returns the changes (createLayout with its full design, and any script or fields it adds) instead of undo, with saved: false. For a report, groups (sub-summaries; a date by month, quarter or year), summaryOnly and chart (one point per group) are also taken, and the script sorts by the groups. arrangement copies a picture of a layout: where each thing is, in points from its part's top left, using the file's real fields; it replaces fields, totals and portals.

<a id="change-design"></a>

### `change_design`

Change a database's design: create, rename, change or delete tables, fields, table occurrences, relationships, value lists, custom functions, layouts and scripts. Returns the changes as applied (with ids), and, when they only add things, `undo`: the changes that take them back. With preview: true nothing changes; it returns what the changes would do, one line each, to show the person first.

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `changes` | array of object of any | yes | Design changes, applied in order as one unit (all or none). Name things by name or id. Ops: - {op:"createTable", name, fields?: [FieldSpec]} also adds a table occurrence and a form layout named after it (withLayout:false to skip) - {op:"renameTable", table, name} / {op:"deleteTable", table} - {op:"createField", table, ...FieldSpec} / {op:"updateField", table, field, ...changes} / {op:"deleteField", table, field} - {op:"createTheme", name, from?: theme to copy, content?: {defaults, styles, contextual?} to import} / {op:"updateTheme", theme, name?, defaults?: {elementType: [StyleRule] \| null}} / {op:"deleteTheme", theme}   (refused while layouts use it). StyleRule: {part: 1 object\|2 text\|4 icon, state: 1 normal\|2 hover\|3 pressed\|4 focus, css: {property: value}}.   Element types: 20 layout background, 34 body, 32 header, 38 footer, 61 edit box, 62 pop-up menu, 64 checkbox set, 70 text, 80 button, 83 portal, 51 rectangle... - {op:"createStyle", theme, name, element, rules?} / {op:"updateStyle", theme, style, element?, name?, rules?} (renaming updates objects using it)   / {op:"deleteStyle", theme, style, element?} (objects using it get the element's default look). Objects use a style with style.name on their layout. - Phone layouts (not in FileMaker): {op:"createLayout", name, phoneOf: layout, width?: 390} makes one from a desktop layout (stacked, tap-sized) that follows its changes until edited by hand; {op:"updateLayout", layout, rebuildPhone: true} rebuilds it. - Layout components (not in FileMaker): {op:"createComponent", name, objects: [LayoutObject]} or {op:"createComponent", name, layout, objectIds: [ids of   objects on it]} (those objects become its first placed copy there) / {op:"updateComponent", component, name?, objects?} (every placed copy follows) /   {op:"deleteComponent", component} (copies stay as plain groups). Place one with a group object {kind:"group", type:8, bounds (top left is where it goes),   component:{id}} in an updateLayout: its children are filled in from the component. Drop "component" from a copy to detach it. get_design lists components. - {op:"restoreDeleted", deleted: id} brings back a deleted table or field (ids in get_design's "deleted"), with its data and the formulas,   relationships and occurrences the delete changed   FieldSpec: {name, type?: text\|number\|date\|time\|timestamp\|container, kind?: normal\|calculation\|summary, calculation?: formula,   calculationContext?: occurrence, comment?, options?: {global?, unstored?, repetitions?, index?: minimal\|all (null: none), noAutoIndex?,   indexLanguage?: English\|Unicode_Raw\|..., externalStorage?: {directory?: base directory id (0 default), secure?: true, fewerFolders?, path?: formula (open storage)}   (containers; kept for FileMaker, tabularius keeps the data in the database), autoEnter?: {serial?: {next, increment, onCommit?},   data?, lastVisited?: true (a new record copies it from the record the window was on), value?: creationTimestamp\|modificationAccountName\|..., calculation?: true (calculation is an auto-enter calc), replaceExisting?,   lookup?: {occurrence, field, from?: occurrence of this table, noMatch?: keep\|lower\|higher\|value\|empty (lower/higher: the next match value down or up), value?, copyEmpty?} (copy from the first related record   when the match fields change), prohibitModification?: true (people can't change it, scripts can)},   validation?: {notEmpty?, unique?, existing?, type?: number\|date4\|time (strict data type), valueList?: name, range?: {min, max}, maxLength?,   calculation?, calculationAlways? (check it on every commit, not only when the field changed), message?}}, summary?: {type: total\|count\|average\|..., field}} - {op:"createOccurrence", name, table \| file: data source, externalTable: the table's id in that file} / {op:"updateOccurrence", occurrence, name?, table?, color?} / {op:"deleteOccurrence", occurrence} - {op:"createRelationship", left, right, predicates: [{left: field, operator?: = ≠ < ≤ > ≥ ×, right: field}]} (left/right are occurrences)   plus per-side options leftCreate/rightCreate (allow creating records on that side through the relationship; new ones default to true)   and leftDelete/rightDelete (delete that side's related records when a record on the other side is deleted)   / {op:"updateRelationship", relationship: id, ...} / {op:"deleteRelationship", relationship: id} - {op:"createValueList", name, values} or {op:"createValueList", name, field: {occurrence, field, second?: field to show too,   showSecondOnly?, sortBySecond?, related?: occurrence (only values related to the current record, starting from it)}}   or {op:"createValueList", name, external: {file: data source, valueList: the list's id in that file}} (a list of another hosted file)   / updateValueList (valueList; values or field replaces the other) / deleteValueList (valueList) - {op:"createCustomFunction", name, parameters, formula, language?: "calculation" (default) \| "javascript"} / updateCustomFunction /   deleteCustomFunction (customFunction). A JavaScript function's formula is the body of a JavaScript function of its parameters   (it returns the answer: a number, text, true/false, or an object/array as JSON text; dates come in as ISO text). It runs in a   sandbox with no files, network, modules or timers, 1 second and 64 MB per call; use it for what calculations do badly   (regular expressions, parsing, hashing, number crunching), not for anything needing the file's data beyond its arguments. - {op:"createCustomMenu", name, installWhen?, items?: [{kind?: command\|submenu\|separator, command?: name (e.g. "New Record") or id,   script?, parameter?, submenu?: menu, title?: formula, installWhen?: formula, shortcut?: {key, modifiers?: 1 Shift + 4 Cmd/Ctrl}}]}   / updateCustomMenu (customMenu; items replaces the list) / deleteCustomMenu (customMenu) - {op:"createMenuSet", name, menus: [menu, ...] in menu bar order} / updateMenuSet (menuSet) / deleteMenuSet (menuSet)   / {op:"setDefaultMenuSet", menuSet} (null for FileMaker's standard menus)   A layout's own menu set: updateLayout with design: {menuSetId} (a set's id, 1 for FileMaker's standard menus, 0 for the file's default).   Layout Setup: design: {viewsAllowed?: [form, list, table], saveRecordChanges?, fieldFrames?, recordIndicator?} (false turns one off; all on by default),   printColumns?: {count: 1-99, order?: across\|down} (records print side by side in Preview mode and PDFs),   fixedMargins?: {top, left, bottom, right} in points (Use fixed page margins: they replace the file's page setup margins in Preview mode and PDFs; null clears it).   Responsive (tabularius only): design: {responsive: {stackBelow: width}} stacks each part in one column in narrower web client windows (a layout without it follows the server's setting, 640 points unless changed; stackBelow 0 never stacks that layout); an object's responsive: {hideBelow: width} hides it there. - {op:"createDataSource", name, paths: ["file:Name"]} (Manage External Data Sources: a FileMaker file, paths tried in order:   file:, fmnet:/host/Name, filemac:, filewin:; or one odbc:DSN entry) / updateDataSource (dataSource; name?, paths?) / deleteDataSource   (refused while occurrences or scripts use it). Nothing connects out: a file reference finds the hosted database of that name. - {op:"setFileOptions", openLayout?, onFirstWindowOpen?: script, onLastWindowClose?: script, onWindowOpen?: script, onWindowClose?: script} (File Options; null clears one) - {op:"createContainerDirectory", path} / {op:"updateContainerDirectory", directory: id, path} / {op:"deleteContainerDirectory", directory}   (Manage Containers base directories, relative to the database's folder; 0 is the default; refused while fields store there) - {op:"createLayout", name, occurrence, design?} (no design: a generated form) / {op:"updateLayout", layout, name?, occurrence?, design?} / deleteLayout - {op:"createScript", name, text} / {op:"updateScript", script, name?, text?, limits?: {steps?, seconds?, loopPasses?} \| null} / deleteScript.   limits is Tabularius's runaway guard for that script (whole numbers; null takes it off). text is the script as FileMaker's   workspace shows it (get_script's text): one step per line, e.g. Set Field [ Table::Field ; formula ], Go to Layout [ “Name” ],   Perform Script [ “Name” ; Parameter: formula ], If [ test ] ... End If, // disables, # comments. Unchanged lines keep their steps.   (steps: [{name, params}] also works.) - {op:"setOrder", list: "layouts"\|"scripts", order: [{item: name}, {folder: "Name", children: [...]}, {separator: true}]}: the list's   order with folders, as Manage Layouts / Manage Scripts show it (layoutOrder / scriptOrder in get_design). Items left out go at the end. Renaming a field or occurrence rewrites every formula, layout and script that refers to it. Stored calculations are computed for existing records. (at least 1 items) |
| `preview` | boolean | no | Describe what the changes would do, without making them (default false) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "change_design",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "changes": [
      {
        "op": "createField",
        "table": "Invoices",
        "name": "DueDate",
        "type": "date"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "applied": [
    {
      "op": "createField",
      "table": 130,
      "name": "DueDate",
      "type": "date",
      "id": 5
    }
  ],
  "undo": [
    {
      "op": "deleteField",
      "table": 130,
      "field": 5
    }
  ]
}
```

With preview: true nothing changes and the result is {lines, layouts?: [{name, issues}]}. Applied changes are recorded in the design history under the account "AI".

<a id="check-formula"></a>

### `check_formula`

Check a calculation formula before using it in change_design, as FileMaker's Specify Calculation dialog does: syntax, field and table occurrence names, function names and parameter counts. Returns {ok:true} or the first error with its offset.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `formula` | string | yes | The formula to check, as typed in Specify Calculation |
| `occurrence` | string | no | Table occurrence it is evaluated from (unqualified names are its fields) |
| `table` | string | no | Or a base table: its first occurrence |
| `customFunction` | string | no | Or the custom function whose body this is (its parameters are known names) |
| `parameters` | array of string | no | A new custom function's parameters |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "check_formula",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "formula": "Totl * 1.2",
    "table": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "code": 102,
  "message": "The field \"Totl\" cannot be found",
  "at": 0
}
```

A formula that checks out returns {"ok": true}.

<a id="design-history"></a>

### `design_history`

Design changes made to a database in Tabularius (by people, scripts or AI), oldest first.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `limit` | integer | no | Most changes to return (default 100, min 1, max 1000) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "design_history",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "limit": 1
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
[
  {
    "seq": 5,
    "at": "2026-10-13T00:07:21.417Z",
    "account": "AI",
    "op": {
      "op": "createTheme",
      "name": "House"
    }
  }
]
```

<a id="audit-log"></a>

### `audit_log`

Who created, changed and deleted which records of a database, and when, oldest first. Edits list each field's old and new value; deletes list the values the record had. Each entry says where the change came from (surface) and the script that made it. Fields named like passwords or keys, and any an administrator excluded, show ‹not logged› instead of a value.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `table` | string | no | Base table name |
| `recordId` | integer | no | Only changes to this record (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |
| `account` | string | no | Only changes made by this account |
| `surface` | string | no | Where the change came from: web, rest (Data API), odata, sql, mcp, admin, automation, hook, cleanup, agent, assistant, import, sync |
| `script` | string | no | Changes a script of this name made |
| `since` | string | no | ISO date or time |
| `limit` | integer | no | Most entries to return (default 100, min 1, max 1000) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "audit_log",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "table": "Invoices",
    "recordId": 12
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
[
  {
    "seq": 9,
    "at": "2026-10-13T00:09:01.953Z",
    "account": "Admin",
    "kind": "create",
    "table": "Invoices",
    "recordId": 12,
    "changes": {
      "Number": "A-12",
      "Total": 250
    }
  },
  {
    "seq": 10,
    "at": "2026-10-13T00:09:01.969Z",
    "account": "Admin",
    "kind": "update",
    "table": "Invoices",
    "recordId": 12,
    "changes": {
      "Total": [
        250,
        275
      ]
    }
  }
]
```

Values of fields named like secrets are shown as "‹hidden from AI tools›".

<a id="explain-record-history"></a>

### `explain_record_history`

What changed on one record and why, newest first: changes made together are one event (who, when, each field from and to), each change says how it came about where the design shows it (worked out by an auto-enter calculation from another field changed then, stamped with the modification time or account, looked up from a related record), which automation or data cleanup made it, and what else the same account changed in other tables at that moment. Works for deleted records too. Use it for "who changed this", "why did Status change", "what happened to this record".

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `table` | string | no | Base table name (or pass layout instead) |
| `layout` | string | no | A layout on the record's table |
| `recordId` | integer | yes | The record to explain (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |
| `limit` | integer | no | Audit entries to read, newest (default 200) (min 1, max 2000) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "explain_record_history",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "recordId": 12
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "table": "Invoices",
  "recordId": 12,
  "events": [
    {
      "at": "2026-10-13T00:09:01.969Z",
      "account": "Admin",
      "kind": "changed",
      "changes": [
        {
          "field": "Total",
          "from": 250,
          "to": 275
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "at": "2026-10-13T00:09:01.953Z",
      "account": "Admin",
      "kind": "created",
      "changes": [
        {
          "field": "Number",
          "to": "A-12"
        },
        {
          "field": "Total",
          "to": 250
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "note": "Newest first. \"how\" says what the file's design shows about a change (auto-enter calculations, stamps, lookups); \"by\" names an automation or data cleanup that ran at that moment. A change with neither was typed, imported or set by a script or API call. The audit log reaches back only as far as it is kept."
}
```

Name the table, or a layout on it.

<a id="suggest-indexes"></a>

### `suggest_indexes`

Slow finds on this server and what would speed them up: each kind of find (table, fields searched, sort) that took 50 ms or more on average since the server started, with its timings, an index to add where a stored field has none (with why), and plain-English hints where no index helps (unstored calculations, criteria starting with *). Read-only: an index is added from the admin console's Slow finds list.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "suggest_indexes",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "finds": [
    {
      "file": "Invoices",
      "table": "Invoices",
      "layout": "Invoices",
      "fields": [
        "Status"
      ],
      "sort": [
        "Number"
      ],
      "count": 14,
      "averageMs": 90,
      "maxMs": 210,
      "totalMs": 1260,
      "records": 24,
      "summary": "Finds in Invoices by Status, sorted by Number took 90 ms on average (longest 210 ms) over 14 finds, on 24 records.",
      "suggestions": [
        {
          "kind": "index",
          "table": "Invoices",
          "field": "Status",
          "why": "An index on Invoices::Status lets finds on it skip reading all 24 records (it helps exact matches (==), ranges and \"begins with\"; word finds already use the word index)."
        },
        {
          "kind": "index",
          "table": "Invoices",
          "field": "Number",
          "why": "An index on Invoices::Number lets sorts on it skip reading all 24 records."
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "note": "Slowest in total first."
}
```

Read-only: nothing is indexed. With no slow finds the result is {"finds": [], "note": "No slow finds since the server started."}.

<a id="get-security"></a>

### `get_security`

Accounts and privilege sets, as Manage Security shows them: each account's privilege set, whether it has a password (blankPassword: still the file's empty one), a second factor, is external or inactive; each privilege set's record, layout, value list and script access and extended privileges; the password policy; and API tokens (without their secrets). importApproximations lists sets imported from the FileMaker file whose access here only approximates FileMaker's (more or less, as each note says; editedSince: changed here since, so the notes may no longer hold): mention it when saying who can see what. Never passwords.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "get_security",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "accounts": [
    {
      "name": "Admin",
      "hasPassword": true,
      "privilegeSet": "[Full Access]",
      "hasTotp": false,
      "blankPassword": false,
      "unmigrated": false
    },
    {
      "name": "Clerk",
      "hasPassword": true,
      "privilegeSet": "Clerks",
      "hasTotp": false,
      "blankPassword": false,
      "unmigrated": false
    }
  ],
  "privilegeSets": [
    {
      "name": "[Full Access]",
      "id": 1,
      "records": {
        "view": true,
        "edit": true,
        "create": true,
        "delete": true
      },
      "layouts": "modifiable",
      "valueLists": "modifiable",
      "scripts": "modifiable",
      "extendedPrivileges": [
        "fmapp",
        "fmwebdirect",
        "fmrest"
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "Clerks",
      "records": {
        "view": true,
        "edit": true,
        "create": true,
        "delete": false
      },
      "layouts": "viewOnly",
      "valueLists": "viewOnly",
      "scripts": "viewOnly",
      "extendedPrivileges": [
        "fmapp"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "passwordPolicy": {},
  "minPasswordLength": 12,
  "apiTokens": []
}
```

API tokens are listed without their ids or secrets.

<a id="review-privileges"></a>

### `review_privileges`

A privilege audit in plain English: risky setups among the accounts and privilege sets, worst first, each as a sentence with where it is and what to do: full-access accounts with no password or only a password, guest access, extended privileges (Data API, OData, ODBC, ...) switched on that no recent sign-in uses, record-level limits that are true for every record, and unstored calculations a limited set can see that read records it can't view. Plus the security health counts (dormant accounts, broad API tokens, sets that over-share). Read-only; never passwords or record values.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `unusedDays` | integer | no | Days without a sign-in that count as unused (default 90) (min 1, max 3650) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "review_privileges",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "findings": [
    {
      "severity": "medium",
      "kind": "full-access-no-2fa",
      "account": "Admin",
      "privilegeSet": "[Full Access]",
      "title": "\"Admin\" has full access with only a password.",
      "detail": "A guessed or leaked password is enough to take over the file. Set up two-factor sign-in for it in Manage Security, or turn on \"require two-factor\" for full-access accounts."
    },
    {
      "severity": "medium",
      "kind": "unused-extended",
      "privilegeSet": "Clerks",
      "title": "\"Clerks\" opens FileMaker-style app sign-in, but none of its 1 account (Clerk) has signed in for 90 days.",
      "detail": "Each surface switched on is a way in. Turn these extended privileges off in Manage Security until someone needs them."
    }
  ],
  "counts": {
    "high": 0,
    "medium": 2,
    "low": 0
  },
  "unusedDays": 90,
  "health": {
    "fullAccessAccounts": [
      "Admin"
    ],
    "without2fa": [
      "Admin",
      "Clerk"
    ],
    "dormant": [
      "Admin",
      "Clerk"
    ],
    "broadTokens": [],
    "oversharingSets": [],
    "orphanedAccessKeys": []
  }
}
```

<a id="check-change-impact"></a>

### `check_change_impact`

Before renaming or deleting a field, table, layout, value list or script: everything that uses it and whether each use breaks. Calculations, scripts, layouts, relationships and value lists in the file (references by id follow a rename; names inside quotes, as in GetField, ExecuteSQL, Evaluate or steps "by name", do not), privilege set entries and record limits that name it (kept by name, so a rename leaves them behind), other hosted files that reach into it (their occurrences, relationships, script calls and value lists, by id: a rename follows, a delete breaks), and Data API clients seen in the server log calling it in the last 30 days. Returns plain sentences first. Read-only.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `kind` | "field" \\| "table" \\| "layout" \\| "script" \\| "valueList" | yes | What is being renamed or deleted |
| `name` | string | yes | The name; a field as Table::Field |
| `change` | "rename" \\| "delete" | no | Default rename |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "check_change_impact",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "kind": "field",
    "name": "Invoices::Status",
    "change": "rename"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "target": {
    "kind": "field",
    "name": "Invoices::Status"
  },
  "change": "rename",
  "uses": [
    {
      "where": "Script \"Mark paid\", line 1",
      "text": "Set Field [ Invoices::Status ; \"Paid\" ]",
      "breaks": false,
      "why": "It refers to it by id and follows the rename."
    },
    {
      "where": "Layout \"Invoices\"",
      "text": "field Invoices::Status",
      "breaks": false,
      "why": "It refers to it by id and follows the rename."
    }
  ],
  "useCount": 2,
  "privileges": [],
  "clients": [],
  "crossFile": [],
  "logDays": 30,
  "logRead": true,
  "summary": [
    "2 other uses in the file follow the rename.",
    "OData and ODBC clients are not logged, so they were not checked."
  ]
}
```

Other hosted files are checked too; one with AI turned off (or that uses such a file) is only counted, never named.

<a id="suggest-rules"></a>

### `suggest_rules`

Rules a table's data already follows, as field options to add: a text field that only ever holds a handful of values (a value list to check entries against; spellings that differ only in case are named), an id-like field that is different on every record (unique, required), a name or key field always filled in (required), a text field holding only numbers, a number counting up with each record (serial), a value nearly every record has (a default). Each has the design changes that add it (propose them with propose_design_change or apply with change_design, one at a time, after the developer agrees). Read-only; skips fields named like secrets and housekeeping fields (creation/modification stamps, cached copies, globals).

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `table` | string | no | One table; default every table |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "suggest_rules",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "table": "Invoices"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "suggestions": [
    {
      "table": "Invoices",
      "field": "Number",
      "kind": "unique",
      "title": "Invoices::Number is different on every record: require a value, and unique values.",
      "evidence": "24 different values in all 24 records.",
      "changes": [
        {
          "op": "updateField",
          "table": "Invoices",
          "field": "Number",
          "options": {
            "validation": {
              "unique": true,
              "notEmpty": true
            }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "alsoAlwaysFilled": [
    {
      "table": "Invoices",
      "fields": [
        "Total",
        "CustomerId",
        "Status"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "tablesChecked": [
    "Invoices"
  ]
}
```

Read-only. A table needs at least 20 records before anything is suggested for it.

<a id="edit-layout-objects"></a>

### `edit_layout_objects`

Change some of a layout's objects without sending its whole design (get_layout_design gives object ids): set properties of objects by id (bounds, text, field, style, conditions, button action, an object's own script triggers...), add objects, remove objects, and replace the layout's own script triggers (OnRecordLoad, OnLayoutEnter, ...). Applied as one change: all or none.

**Hints:** destructive

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `layout` | string or integer | yes | The layout's name or id |
| `set` | array of object | no | Properties to change on existing objects; nested objects (in portals, tabs, groups) are found by id too |
| `set[].object` | integer | yes | (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |
| `set[].changes` | object of any | yes |  |
| `add` | array of object of any | no | New objects, shaped like get_layout_design's (kind, bounds {top,left,bottom,right}, ...); parent: id of a portal, tab panel or group to put one in |
| `remove` | array of integer | no | Ids of objects to delete (with what they contain) |
| `triggers` | array of object | no | The layout's triggers, replacing the current ones ([] removes them all) |
| `triggers[].event` | string | yes |  |
| `triggers[].script` | string or integer | yes |  |
| `triggers[].parameter` | string | no |  |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "edit_layout_objects",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "set": [
      {
        "object": 1,
        "changes": {
          "text": "Invoice"
        }
      }
    ],
    "triggers": [
      {
        "event": "OnRecordLoad",
        "script": "Mark paid"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "layout": "Invoices",
  "objects": 9,
  "triggers": [
    {
      "event": "OnRecordLoad",
      "scriptId": 1,
      "script": "Mark paid"
    }
  ]
}
```

objects is the number of top-level objects on the layout afterwards. The change is recorded in the design history under the account "AI".

<a id="try-design-change"></a>

### `try_design_change`

Try design changes (change_design's) on a throwaway copy of the file, then run scripts there once, offline (no network, mail or plug-ins), and report how each run went: steps, the last error and where. Nothing changes in the real file. By default the scripts the changes create or rewrite are run.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `changes` | array of object of any | yes | Design changes, applied in order as one unit (all or none). Name things by name or id. Ops: - {op:"createTable", name, fields?: [FieldSpec]} also adds a table occurrence and a form layout named after it (withLayout:false to skip) - {op:"renameTable", table, name} / {op:"deleteTable", table} - {op:"createField", table, ...FieldSpec} / {op:"updateField", table, field, ...changes} / {op:"deleteField", table, field} - {op:"createTheme", name, from?: theme to copy, content?: {defaults, styles, contextual?} to import} / {op:"updateTheme", theme, name?, defaults?: {elementType: [StyleRule] \| null}} / {op:"deleteTheme", theme}   (refused while layouts use it). StyleRule: {part: 1 object\|2 text\|4 icon, state: 1 normal\|2 hover\|3 pressed\|4 focus, css: {property: value}}.   Element types: 20 layout background, 34 body, 32 header, 38 footer, 61 edit box, 62 pop-up menu, 64 checkbox set, 70 text, 80 button, 83 portal, 51 rectangle... - {op:"createStyle", theme, name, element, rules?} / {op:"updateStyle", theme, style, element?, name?, rules?} (renaming updates objects using it)   / {op:"deleteStyle", theme, style, element?} (objects using it get the element's default look). Objects use a style with style.name on their layout. - Phone layouts (not in FileMaker): {op:"createLayout", name, phoneOf: layout, width?: 390} makes one from a desktop layout (stacked, tap-sized) that follows its changes until edited by hand; {op:"updateLayout", layout, rebuildPhone: true} rebuilds it. - Layout components (not in FileMaker): {op:"createComponent", name, objects: [LayoutObject]} or {op:"createComponent", name, layout, objectIds: [ids of   objects on it]} (those objects become its first placed copy there) / {op:"updateComponent", component, name?, objects?} (every placed copy follows) /   {op:"deleteComponent", component} (copies stay as plain groups). Place one with a group object {kind:"group", type:8, bounds (top left is where it goes),   component:{id}} in an updateLayout: its children are filled in from the component. Drop "component" from a copy to detach it. get_design lists components. - {op:"restoreDeleted", deleted: id} brings back a deleted table or field (ids in get_design's "deleted"), with its data and the formulas,   relationships and occurrences the delete changed   FieldSpec: {name, type?: text\|number\|date\|time\|timestamp\|container, kind?: normal\|calculation\|summary, calculation?: formula,   calculationContext?: occurrence, comment?, options?: {global?, unstored?, repetitions?, index?: minimal\|all (null: none), noAutoIndex?,   indexLanguage?: English\|Unicode_Raw\|..., externalStorage?: {directory?: base directory id (0 default), secure?: true, fewerFolders?, path?: formula (open storage)}   (containers; kept for FileMaker, tabularius keeps the data in the database), autoEnter?: {serial?: {next, increment, onCommit?},   data?, lastVisited?: true (a new record copies it from the record the window was on), value?: creationTimestamp\|modificationAccountName\|..., calculation?: true (calculation is an auto-enter calc), replaceExisting?,   lookup?: {occurrence, field, from?: occurrence of this table, noMatch?: keep\|lower\|higher\|value\|empty (lower/higher: the next match value down or up), value?, copyEmpty?} (copy from the first related record   when the match fields change), prohibitModification?: true (people can't change it, scripts can)},   validation?: {notEmpty?, unique?, existing?, type?: number\|date4\|time (strict data type), valueList?: name, range?: {min, max}, maxLength?,   calculation?, calculationAlways? (check it on every commit, not only when the field changed), message?}}, summary?: {type: total\|count\|average\|..., field}} - {op:"createOccurrence", name, table \| file: data source, externalTable: the table's id in that file} / {op:"updateOccurrence", occurrence, name?, table?, color?} / {op:"deleteOccurrence", occurrence} - {op:"createRelationship", left, right, predicates: [{left: field, operator?: = ≠ < ≤ > ≥ ×, right: field}]} (left/right are occurrences)   plus per-side options leftCreate/rightCreate (allow creating records on that side through the relationship; new ones default to true)   and leftDelete/rightDelete (delete that side's related records when a record on the other side is deleted)   / {op:"updateRelationship", relationship: id, ...} / {op:"deleteRelationship", relationship: id} - {op:"createValueList", name, values} or {op:"createValueList", name, field: {occurrence, field, second?: field to show too,   showSecondOnly?, sortBySecond?, related?: occurrence (only values related to the current record, starting from it)}}   or {op:"createValueList", name, external: {file: data source, valueList: the list's id in that file}} (a list of another hosted file)   / updateValueList (valueList; values or field replaces the other) / deleteValueList (valueList) - {op:"createCustomFunction", name, parameters, formula, language?: "calculation" (default) \| "javascript"} / updateCustomFunction /   deleteCustomFunction (customFunction). A JavaScript function's formula is the body of a JavaScript function of its parameters   (it returns the answer: a number, text, true/false, or an object/array as JSON text; dates come in as ISO text). It runs in a   sandbox with no files, network, modules or timers, 1 second and 64 MB per call; use it for what calculations do badly   (regular expressions, parsing, hashing, number crunching), not for anything needing the file's data beyond its arguments. - {op:"createCustomMenu", name, installWhen?, items?: [{kind?: command\|submenu\|separator, command?: name (e.g. "New Record") or id,   script?, parameter?, submenu?: menu, title?: formula, installWhen?: formula, shortcut?: {key, modifiers?: 1 Shift + 4 Cmd/Ctrl}}]}   / updateCustomMenu (customMenu; items replaces the list) / deleteCustomMenu (customMenu) - {op:"createMenuSet", name, menus: [menu, ...] in menu bar order} / updateMenuSet (menuSet) / deleteMenuSet (menuSet)   / {op:"setDefaultMenuSet", menuSet} (null for FileMaker's standard menus)   A layout's own menu set: updateLayout with design: {menuSetId} (a set's id, 1 for FileMaker's standard menus, 0 for the file's default).   Layout Setup: design: {viewsAllowed?: [form, list, table], saveRecordChanges?, fieldFrames?, recordIndicator?} (false turns one off; all on by default),   printColumns?: {count: 1-99, order?: across\|down} (records print side by side in Preview mode and PDFs),   fixedMargins?: {top, left, bottom, right} in points (Use fixed page margins: they replace the file's page setup margins in Preview mode and PDFs; null clears it).   Responsive (tabularius only): design: {responsive: {stackBelow: width}} stacks each part in one column in narrower web client windows (a layout without it follows the server's setting, 640 points unless changed; stackBelow 0 never stacks that layout); an object's responsive: {hideBelow: width} hides it there. - {op:"createDataSource", name, paths: ["file:Name"]} (Manage External Data Sources: a FileMaker file, paths tried in order:   file:, fmnet:/host/Name, filemac:, filewin:; or one odbc:DSN entry) / updateDataSource (dataSource; name?, paths?) / deleteDataSource   (refused while occurrences or scripts use it). Nothing connects out: a file reference finds the hosted database of that name. - {op:"setFileOptions", openLayout?, onFirstWindowOpen?: script, onLastWindowClose?: script, onWindowOpen?: script, onWindowClose?: script} (File Options; null clears one) - {op:"createContainerDirectory", path} / {op:"updateContainerDirectory", directory: id, path} / {op:"deleteContainerDirectory", directory}   (Manage Containers base directories, relative to the database's folder; 0 is the default; refused while fields store there) - {op:"createLayout", name, occurrence, design?} (no design: a generated form) / {op:"updateLayout", layout, name?, occurrence?, design?} / deleteLayout - {op:"createScript", name, text} / {op:"updateScript", script, name?, text?, limits?: {steps?, seconds?, loopPasses?} \| null} / deleteScript.   limits is Tabularius's runaway guard for that script (whole numbers; null takes it off). text is the script as FileMaker's   workspace shows it (get_script's text): one step per line, e.g. Set Field [ Table::Field ; formula ], Go to Layout [ “Name” ],   Perform Script [ “Name” ; Parameter: formula ], If [ test ] ... End If, // disables, # comments. Unchanged lines keep their steps.   (steps: [{name, params}] also works.) - {op:"setOrder", list: "layouts"\|"scripts", order: [{item: name}, {folder: "Name", children: [...]}, {separator: true}]}: the list's   order with folders, as Manage Layouts / Manage Scripts show it (layoutOrder / scriptOrder in get_design). Items left out go at the end. Renaming a field or occurrence rewrites every formula, layout and script that refers to it. Stored calculations are computed for existing records. |
| `scripts` | array of string | no | Scripts to run on the copy (default: those the changes write, up to 5) (at most 5 items) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "try_design_change",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "changes": [
      {
        "op": "updateScript",
        "script": "Mark paid",
        "text": "Set Field [ Invoices::Status ; \"Paid\" ]"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "applies": true,
  "runs": [
    {
      "script": "Mark paid",
      "run": {
        "outcome": "ok",
        "error": 0,
        "steps": 1,
        "layout": "Invoices"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Changes that would not apply are refused with the error before anything runs. The real file is not changed.

<a id="paste-from-filemaker"></a>

### `paste_from_filemaker`

Read what was copied in FileMaker Pro (clipboard XML: tables, fields, scripts, script steps, custom functions, value lists, or layout objects) and return it as Tabularius changes, not applied: change_design applies design changes; layout objects go in with edit_layout_objects add. Comes with notes on anything that did not carry over.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `xml` | string | yes | The <fmxmlsnippet> XML |
| `table` | string or integer | no | Table to paste fields into |
| `script` | string or integer | no | Script to paste steps into |
| `at` | integer | no | Step index to insert pasted steps at (default the end) (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |
| `layout` | string or integer | no | Layout that layout objects go on (its theme names the styles) |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "paste_from_filemaker",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "table": "Invoices",
    "xml": "<fmxmlsnippet type=\"FMObjectList\"><Field id=\"7\" dataType=\"Text\" fieldType=\"Normal\" name=\"Notes\"/></fmxmlsnippet>"
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "changes": [
    {
      "op": "createField",
      "table": 130,
      "name": "Notes",
      "type": "text",
      "kind": "normal"
    }
  ],
  "summary": [
    "1 field"
  ],
  "notes": []
}
```

Nothing is applied: design changes go to change_design. A snippet of layout objects returns objects for edit_layout_objects add instead.

<a id="copy-for-filemaker"></a>

### `copy_for_filemaker`

FileMaker Pro clipboard XML for design items, to paste into a FileMaker file: tables, fields, scripts, custom functions and value lists by id (get_design), or a layout's objects by id.

**Hints:** read-only

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | string | yes | Hosted database name |
| `tables` | array of integer | no | Table ids (from get_design) (at most 500 items) |
| `fields` | object | no | Fields to copy: {table: the table's id, ids: field ids} |
| `fields.table` | integer | yes | (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |
| `fields.ids` | array of integer | yes |  |
| `scripts` | array of integer | no | Script ids |
| `customFunctions` | array of integer | no | Custom function ids |
| `valueLists` | array of integer | no | Value list ids |
| `layout` | string or integer | no | A layout whose objects to copy, by name or id (with the object ids) |
| `objects` | array of integer | no | Object ids on layout |

**Example:**

```json
{
  "name": "copy_for_filemaker",
  "arguments": {
    "database": "Invoices",
    "scripts": [
      1
    ]
  }
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "xml": "<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\"?>\n<fmxmlsnippet type=\"FMObjectList\"><Script includeInMenu=\"True\" runFullAccess=\"False\" id=\"1\" name=\"Mark paid\"><Step enable=\"True\" id=\"76\" name=\"Set Field\"><Calculation><![CDATA[\"Paid\"]]></Calculation><Field table=\"Invoices\" id=\"4\" name=\"Status\"/></Step><Step enable=\"True\" id=\"75\" name=\"Commit Records/Requests\"><NoInteract state=\"True\"/></Step></Script></fmxmlsnippet>",
  "notes": []
}
```

objects needs layout, the layout the objects are on.

The file's image library (button icons and pictures): id, file name, type and size.

<a id="add-image"></a>

### `add_image`

Add an image to the file's library, for buttons and pictures on layouts. Returns its id.

**Permissions:** [Full Access] in the file, or the server administrator; any other privilege set (even one that can modify scripts) is refused, and so is a scoped API token.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

```json
  }
}
```
